The layout # Four layers, all under src/ : src/ glitchygames/ the engine (distribution glitchygames); it has no examples package: every game and demo is a member, and its resources/ holds only what the engine itself ships games/<game>/ one member per game: every game (mr-muncher, clockwork-keep, brave-adventurer, paddleslap, drawing-fire) demos/<demo>/ one member per demo (dt-demo, joystick-demo, text-input-demo): a small program that shows one engine feature (console scripts `dt-demo`, `joystick-demo`, `text-input-demo`; no browser build) apps/<app>/ one member per application (Bitmappy) tests/ the engine's own tests scripts/ tools Nothing at the repository root is importable as one of our packages. Tests and tools run from the root import the installed engine and members ( uv sync installs them editable, nox non-editable), and tests/test_suite_collection.py checks that import glitchygames resolves to the installed package. Coverage maps the installed copies back to src/ ( [tool.coverage.paths] ), so its report names the files in the repository. Two meanings of "demo" # A demo (a demos-layer member): a program under src/demos/<demo>/ , run with its console script or python -m <package> . It is code. A game's bundled demo recording : <package>/demos/<name>.jsonl.gz , package data inside a game (PaddleSlap's rally.jsonl.gz ), replayed by that game's console script. It is data, and glitchygames.bundled_demos finds it (see "Bundled demos" below). A demos directory inside a package is therefore never a demos-layer member, and a demos-layer member's recordings (it has none today) would still be that member's own package data. What a member is # A member is a directory under its layer, named after its distribution (with hyphens), holding: src/games/<game>/ pyproject.toml its metadata (below) README.md one paragraph: what it is, how to play and test it src/<package>/ its import package (underscores: a hyphen cannot be imported), never at the member's root, so nothing in the member directory can be imported by accident in place of the installed package tests/ its tests (no __init__.py), with its golden replay in tests/fixtures/replays/golden.jsonl.gz Its pyproject.toml follows Mr. Muncher's ( src/games/mr-muncher/pyproject.toml ): [project] name = "<distribution>" version = "1.0.0" description = "<one line>" requires-python = ">=3.14,<4.0" dependencies = [ "glitchygames" ] [project.scripts] < console-script > = "<package>:main" [build-system] requires = [ "hatchling" ] build-backend = "hatchling.build" [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages = [ "src/<package>" ] [tool.uv.sources] glitchygames = { workspace = true } A member that reuses another member's code depends on it too ( dependencies = ["glitchygames", "<other>"] , <other> = { workspace = true } ). Files inside the import package (a sprite TOML, a bundled demo) ship as package data: read them through the module's own path ( Path(__file__).parent / 'sprites' ), never through the repository. Working with a member # From the repository root: uv sync --all-extras --all-groups --all-packages # the engine and every member, with the dev tools uv run <console-script> # play it uv run pytest --no-cov src/games/<game>/tests # its tests alone (no coverage gate on a subset) uv run pytest # everything: the engine's and every member's tests A plain uv sync keeps every member installed (each is in the root's dev dependency group), but drops the dev tools: use the full command above. The 100% coverage gate covers the engine and every member together, so it is met only by the whole run. Each layer is also an extra of the engine, naming that layer's members, so an installer picks the engine alone or with them: uv build --all-packages # every wheel, into dist/ # (nox -s build-wheel does the same) pip install --find-links dist glitchygames # the engine pip install --find-links dist "glitchygames[games]" # the engine and every game pip install --find-links dist "glitchygames[demos,apps]" # the engine, the demos and the apps The names are not yet on PyPI (neither glitchygames nor any game's), so install from the built wheels as above: a plain pip install glitchygames would fetch whatever package someone else published under that name. ( uv sync --extra games does the same in the repository.) A layer with no member yet is an empty extra; tests/test_workspace_config.py keeps each extra equal to its layer's members. Recordings name games by logical names : <layer>.<module path inside the package>:<class> ( games.mr_muncher.game:MrMuncherScene ). A recording therefore does not depend on where the code lives, and moving a game changes no recording. The layers are data in the engine, src/glitchygames/logical_names.py : MEMBER_LAYERS for members (kept equal to the workspace by tests/test_workspace_config.py ). Every game, demo and Bitmappy is a member; the engine has no examples package. Golden replays live with the member's tests; the golden plugin collects them from every member, so the engine's uv run pytest replays each one. The browser build ships a member's package as its own archive ( <package>.zip ) beside the engine's glitchygames.zip ( scripts/build_browser_bundle.py , GameSpecification.member_packages ). API reference : scripts/gen_ref_pages.py writes a page per member package ( <package>/index.md ), listed under "Games API Reference" in mkdocs.yml , or under "Apps API Reference" for an app (Bitmappy's bitmappy/index.md ). Wheels : nox -s build-wheel builds the wheel of the engine and of every member ( uv build --all-packages ). Moving a game out of the engine # Historical: every game and demo has moved out and src/glitchygames/examples/ is gone (Part 3, 2026-10-26). A new game or demo starts as a fresh member. These steps record how the moves were done. The recipe Mr. Muncher's move followed ( plans/2026-10-24-workspace-packages-1-foundation.md , Task 9). Do one game per commit series, and verify each before the next. Every step names the check that fails if it is skipped: tests/test_workspace_config.py catches a member left out of any tool's configuration. 1. Move the code and tests # git mv src/glitchygames/examples/<package> src/games/<game>/src/<package> , then delete what is left of the old directory: its git-ignored __pycache__ would otherwise keep an importable namespace package there. git mv of a directory carries its untracked __pycache__ along too: delete it in the member as well (its .pyc files name the old module). Move its tests to src/games/<game>/tests/ with no __init__.py (a tests directory must not be a package named tests : tests/test_suite_collection.py ). pytest imports every test module under its path from the repository root, never its bare file name ( src.games.mr-muncher.tests.test_mr_muncher_maze_and_actors , the same under uv run pytest and nox: --import-mode=importlib without namespace packages, the root on the path, in the root pyproject.toml ), so two members may have test files or helpers of the same name (BUGS.md #224 item 31). To patch a test module's own names, use __name__ ( mocker.patch(f'{__name__}.LOG') ). Name test files after the package by convention, test_<package>_<area>.py (Drawing Fire's test_drawing_fire_battle.py ). A helper module beside the tests is imported by that same path ( from src.apps.bitmappy.tests.film_strip_support import ... ), never by its bare name: tests/test_suite_collection.py::test_no_member_test_imports_a_module_by_a_bare_name fails on one. A member directory whose name holds a dash cannot be named in an import statement: give such a member's shared helpers to its tests as conftest.py fixtures (the simplest), or load one with importlib.import_module('src.games.mr-muncher.tests.maze_support') . A member may have a tests/conftest.py (Drawing Fire's drains the event queue). It is imported by its path too, so nothing may import conftest by name: look a conftest up as pytest registered it, by its path ( pytestconfig.pluginmanager.get_plugin(str(pytestconfig.rootpath / 'conftest.py')) ). Move its golden replay to src/games/<game>/tests/fixtures/replays/golden.jsonl.gz , its bytes unchanged. Data its tests read beside them (golden sounds, for instance) moves with them. Delete the emptied tests/fixtures/replays/<console-script>/ (and any parent it leaves empty: Drawing Fire's move emptied the root's tests/fixtures/ ). Rewrite glitchygames.examples.<package> imports to <package> ( git grep -l across the repository, excluding plans/ ), then read the whole diff: a docstring or a path string can match too. 2. Create the member # src/games/<game>/pyproject.toml (above) and README.md . The package's __init__.py re-exports main . The move's tests, one file per subject, each named test_<distribution with - as _>_<subject>.py ( tests/test_suite_collection.py refuses a test file named for anything else, or a name used twice). A member has only the subjects it has tests for: _logical_names.py : the game's classes keep the logical names its recordings hold (every member has this one); _install_location.py : the package imports from <member>/src/ (or site-packages in a wheel install), and (for a member that was once an example) importlib.util.find_spec('glitchygames.examples') is None, so a leftover ignored directory fails a test. A brand-new member, never an example, has no "old example module is gone" test; _wheel.py : the member's wheel holds only its package, plus its data (sprites, demos, resources); _package_data.py : the member's shipped data (a sprite library, a bundled demo) is inside the package, checked without building a wheel ( _wheel.py is for the tests that build one); _entry_points.py : the console script and python -m <package> resolve to main ; _recording_history.py : the golden's old path maps to its new one in the root pyproject.toml 's [tool.glitchygames] recording-renames (its history follows it), and so does every other moved recording. That is six subjects: logical_names, install_location, wheel, package_data, entry_points, recording_history. A move test outside them goes beside the member's other tests, named for its subject (Brave Adventurer's tests/core/test_brave_adventurer_shared_core.py , for example). 3. Register it in the root configuration # File What to add or change pyproject.toml Remove its console script from [project.scripts] (the member's own pyproject.toml has it now). Add the member to its layer's extra ( games , demos or apps in [project.optional-dependencies] ), [tool.uv.workspace] members , [tool.uv.sources] , the dev dependency group, pytest testpaths , addopts ( --cov=<package> ), coverage source and [tool.coverage.paths] , ruff src , include and namespace-packages (its tests), isort known-first-party , ty root and src.include , deptry known_first_party . Re-key any per-file ruff ignore that names the old path. pyrightconfig.json Add it to include , a tests environment (before the member's own) and the member's environment, each with the extraPaths Mr. Muncher's have. Every member is a src layout, so the environments name the member's src/ ( WorkspaceMember.import_roots in scripts/workspace_packages.py ), as Brave Adventurer's do: that is the one form. tests/test_workspace_config.py::test_every_member_keeps_its_packages_under_src enforces the layout, and no configuration entry may name a member path the workspace does not derive noxfile.py _CODE_DIRS , _SOURCE_PACKAGE_DIRS , _MEMBER_DISTRIBUTIONS wily.cfg The path list mkdocs.yml The mkdocstrings paths , and its API page under "Games API Reference" uv.lock Regenerate: uv lock 4. Update the engine's tables # src/glitchygames/logical_names.py : add its package to MEMBER_LAYERS . Its recordings need nothing else (their logical names do not change); tests/test_logical_names.py pins both tables. The root pyproject.toml 's [tool.glitchygames.recording-renames] : one line per moved recording, old path to new, so its run-ledger history stays connected. Each lookup is one step: a recording that has already moved once needs a line from each of its old paths. 5. Update the scripts and tests that name it # The recording tools are the engine's, and the game has them without declaring anything ( --record-golden-trace , --record-session , --verify , --measure , ..., or glitchygames <tool> : Tools for any game ). What this repository adds is test data and its own tables: scripts/golden_inputs.py : the game's golden input script ( <package>_script ) and controls tail ( <package>_controls ), each a callable taking no arguments that returns an InputScript , importing what it reads of its game inside the function. Any tool reaches them as MODULE:NAME from the repository root ( --input-script scripts.golden_inputs:<package>_script , --controls-tail scripts.golden_inputs:<package>_controls ). scripts/record_golden_traces.py : add a '<module>:<class>' reference to GAME_SCENES (never a module-level import of a member: the subprocess import test fails on one), GAME_MODULES (whose value is the bare package name) and its input script's builder to SCRIPT_BUILDERS . It records on the engine's golden-trace harness ( glitchygames.replay.tools.golden_traces ). scripts/record_scripted_session.py records the golden replay on the engine's scripted-session recorder ( glitchygames.replay.tools.scripted_sessions , the record-session tool). Add the game's controls tail to CONTROLS_TAIL_BUILDERS , and the game to INPUT_ONLY_PLACEMENT_GAMES or POLLED_INPUT_GAMES when its script needs it. It derives its fixture directories from GAME_MODULES and the workspace ( REPLAY_FIXTURE_DIRECTORIES ), and refuses a game no member holds; edit its docstring's commands too. The root pyproject.toml 's [tool.glitchygames] games : add the member's console script, so glitchygames verify and glitchygames measure with no --game take its recordings. tests/replay/test_golden_replays.py : its imports, GAMEPLAY_ACTION_MAPS , ENGINE_SCENE_CONTROLS , UNEXERCISED_CONTROLS and any table naming the game. Engine tests no longer borrow a game, by import or by path: tests/test_suite_collection.py ( engine_test_imports_of_members ) fails on any root test that imports a member. Each kind of test lives in one place: The game's own tests are in the member ( src/games/<game>/tests/ ): its rules, sprites, touch controls, replays and the move's tests above. A test that only the game's code can answer goes there, not in tests/ . Engine tests use stand-ins : tests/stand_in_harness_games.py (games for the replay and harness tests) and tests/stand_in_games.py (games and distributions for the discovery, replay-plugin and playback tests). A test that needs a game, a root-layout example or several console scripts writes or imports a stand-in; it never imports a member. Cross-member tests discover through the workspace ( scripts/workspace_packages.py ) and assert hand-written expectations in tests/workspace_expectations.py ( EXPECTED_GOLDENS , EXPECTED_GAME_CONSOLE_SCRIPTS , EXPECTED_ALL_CONSOLE_SCRIPTS , EXPECTED_BUNDLED_DEMOS ). They are written out on purpose, because an expectation derived from the thing it checks checks nothing. Edit them when a game, golden, bundled demo or console script is added or removed. Also add the game to the control tables in tests/replay/golden_replay_controls.py , and to tests/replay/test_record_scripted_session.py::test_a_member_games_fixture_is_directly_in_the_members_replay_fixtures . The exemptions ( MEMBER_IMPORT_EXEMPT_MODULES and MEMBER_IMPORT_EXEMPT_NAMES in tests/test_suite_collection.py , each with its reason; a stale one fails): the module tests/replay/golden_replay_controls.py , whose per-game control tables are cross-member infrastructure moved there unchanged, and the eleven named imports in tests/world/test_golden_traces.py , whose per-game world rules measure the games' own drawings and players. Nothing else in tests/ may import a member. Every game is a member now (Drawing Fire, the last in the engine's examples, moved), so no game is a root-layout example any more. The root's fixtures/replays/<console-script>/ layout stays only as the replay plugin's layout for other projects; the tests of it ( tests/replay/test_replay_plugin.py , tests/replay/test_golden_replays.py , tests/test_code_tree.py , tests/test_measure_staged_replays.py ) use stand-ins: a tmp_path path, a stand-in installed distribution, a pytester copy. A new game or demo starts as a member; a test that needs a root-layout or several-console-script example writes one. Paths built with / ( ... / 'fixtures' / 'replays' / '<game>' / ... ) escape the grep below: also grep for '<console-script>' / and / '<console-script>' . git grep for the old package path and the old golden path across the repository: engine tests that borrow a game (a collision test using its sprites), benchmarks reading its golden, scripts importing it. Point each at the member, or move the test into the member when it is really the game's. Once done, the only matches left are on purpose: git grep -n \ "glitchygames.examples.<package>\|fixtures/replays/<game>" \ -- ':!plans' ':!quality' ':!BUGS.md' (grep's . matches any character, so the dotted pattern finds the slashed path too) prints only the recording-renames line (the old path is its point) and the member's move tests (the history check on that line in _recording_history.py , the old-package check and docstring in _install_location.py ). plans/ , quality/ (ledger rows) and BUGS.md are history and keep the old paths. 6. The browser build # In scripts/build_browser_bundle.py , its GAMES entry's module becomes <package>.game and member_packages names its package (a tuple, dependencies first); its TOUCH_LAYOUTS entry is unchanged. tests/test_build_browser_bundle.py pins which games ship member packages. A game that depends on another member lists both, the one depended on first: each ships as its own archive. 7. The docs # docs/games/<game>.md : its file table and every path ( src/games/<game>/src/<package>/... ), and an "Its package" line linking here. docs/glitchygames/examples/index.md : remove its ::: block, if it has one (its API page is now generated from the member). README.md and CLAUDE.md : where the game lives. 8. Verify # uv lock # then read its diff: only the new member uv sync --all-extras --all-groups --all-packages uv run --extra dev nox -s format-code lint-code lint-dependencies uv run basedpyright && uv run nox -s static-analysis-ty # The member's tests, its golden replay among them (no -k: a golden's id is # <console-script>/golden, hyphenated, so -k <package> would deselect it) uv run pytest --dummy-only --no-cov -q src/games/<game>/tests # The engine's checks on its golden replay, and its golden trace uv run pytest --dummy-only --no-cov -q \ tests/replay/test_golden_replays.py tests/world/test_golden_traces.py -k <package> # The configuration guards, and every engine test that borrows the game (step 5's git grep) uv run pytest --dummy-only --no-cov -q tests/test_suite_collection.py \ tests/test_workspace_config.py tests/test_workspace_packages.py tests/test_logical_names.py \ tests/test_browser_touch_controls.py tests/test_build_browser_bundle.py \ tests/engine/test_engine_lifecycle.py tests/test_recording_metrics.py \ tests/test_our_measured_recordings.py tests/test_measure_staged_replays.py \ tests/test_generate_performance_graphs.py tests/replay tests/world <borrowing tests> uv run pytest # the whole suite, both drivers, 100% coverage uv run <console-script> --verify # its golden replay and bundled demos, replayed headless uv run glitchygames unmeasured --game <console-script> # what --measure would measure of it uv build --package <distribution> # the member builds on its own uv run python -m scripts.build_browser_bundle <console-script> --output <scratch directory> uv run nox -s browser -- <console-script> # its browser bundle, served and opened uv run nox -s lint-docs # the docs build strictly The bundle built without serving must list <package>.zip in its pyscript.toml , and the member's wheel hold only its package. Before the whole suite, a coverage run of the member's tests and its borrowing tests ( --cov=<package> --cov-fail-under=0 ) shows its code still at 100% from where it now is. The golden replay is not re-recorded: its bytes are unchanged, and it replays strictly from its new place. Its first frame records the scene's module, so its content hash changes: glitchygames report shows that this is the only difference. 9. Commit # The replay-metrics pre-commit hook ( scripts/measure_staged_replays.py , which runs glitchygames unmeasured , then glitchygames measure --code-tree TREE --rows-directory DIR ) measures every recording on the new code and stages the rows (about 12 s). It refuses a commit with untracked files under src/ or a partial commit, so stage the whole move ( git add -A src tests scripts docs ) before committing. Special cases # A member that was never in a layer (Bitmappy, an app that lived in the engine as glitchygames.bitmappy , outside examples/ , so no layer table named it): its logical name changes when it moves, from its module path ( glitchygames.bitmappy.editor:BitmapEditorScene ) to apps.bitmappy.editor:BitmapEditorScene , so a recording made before the move no longer matches. A plain replay refuses such a recording, naming the remedy, and --replay-trace OLD --rebaseline NEW --headless converts it (a rebaseline compares the game and each scene by qualified name alone and writes the current logical names: gameplay replay ). A game that was already in a layer keeps its logical name when it moves, as the recipe above says. Bitmappy has no golden replay, so its move converted none; it keeps its tests named test_bitmappy_*.py , its sprite library as package data ( bitmappy.SPRITE_CONFIG_DIR ), and its member declares everything it imports itself (the engine's pyproject.toml no longer lists tenacity, for instance). Several games in one project (Brave Adventurer and its Egyptian edition, Papyrus): one member, built and published together, with layered import packages in its own src layout ( src/games/brave-adventurer/src/ ): the primitives both games share ( brave_adventurer_core ), each game on top of them ( brave_adventurer , brave_adventurer_papyrus ), and a launcher ( brave_adventurer_modes ) as the member's one console script. The launcher starts the game a recording's header names, so the golden-replay plugin's one console script per member replays every game's golden; the goldens are named apart ( golden-<game>.jsonl.gz ). A member that keeps several console scripts instead has each recording replayed through the one whose entry point's module holds the game its header names ( src/glitchygames/replay/tools/children.py , recorded_games_console_script ). scripts/record_scripted_session.py names each such game's golden ( GOLDEN_FIXTURE_NAMES ) and keys its console scripts by game ( GAME_CONSOLE_SCRIPTS ), as tests/replay/test_golden_replays.py keys each golden's controls: one script can replay several games' goldens. Share only by mechanical moves: recordings and golden traces name sprites by class name and creation order, so a class may change module but not name, and nothing may be created in a different order. Its browser bundle lists every archive a game needs, the shared ones first. A game that is one module (PaddleSlap's paddleslap.py ): its recordings name games.paddleslap:Game , so Game must stay defined in the package itself ( src/paddleslap/__init__.py ), not in a paddleslap/game.py it re-exports: a re-export does not change Game.__module__ , and the logical name would become games.paddleslap.game:Game . Ruff's non-empty-init-module (RUF067) is ignored for that file in pyproject.toml . A package's __init__ never runs as __main__ , so the module's if __name__ == '__main__' moves to src/<package>/__main__.py ( python -m paddleslap , as it was when the game lived in the engine's examples package). Bundled demos ship inside the package as package data, <package>/demos/<name>.jsonl.gz (PaddleSlap's paddleslap/demos/rally.jsonl.gz , read through Path(__file__).parent ). The engine finds them in the installed packages: glitchygames.bundled_demos.bundled_demos() ( find_spec over the packages its caller names, with no default; bookmarked copies left out) returns BundledDemo records (console script, installed path, install name). It is the one lookup: the replay plugin's bundled_demo_paths (which raises for a demo no console script replays) and glitchygames.replay.tools.recordings.game_recordings (a game's own demos, which --verify and --measure take) both call it. Development installs are editable ( uv sync , and the replay-metrics nox session's uv run --all-packages ), so the demos are found in the repository and the ledger names them by repository path; under a built install ( site-packages , as nox's test sessions install on purpose) a recording outside the repository is named by its install name ( glitchygames.replay.tools.measure.recording_ledger_name ). A demo moved twice needs a recording-renames line from each old path. Engine-private names : a member uses only the engine's public API. Where a game reaches into the engine, give the engine a public read-only API first, then move the game. PaddleSlap needed no private name once the engine offered BallSprite.trajectory and record_trajectory_point . A known exemption, member tests : a member's tests may use the engine's test seams (for example SceneManager._reset and FontManager._font_cache , which reset engine state between tests); the member's game code may not. A public testing helper for them is a follow-up ( plans/future-features.md , item #56). Pitfalls # A plain uv sync drops the dev tools (pytest among them): use uv sync --all-extras --all-groups --all-packages . A member-only test run fails the coverage gate: add --no-cov , and let the whole run check coverage. An old example directory left on disk (its ignored __pycache__ ) is importable and shadows the member, and tests/test_suite_collection.py rejects a glitchygames/ directory at the root. Delete leftovers after moving. The same trap applies to Bitmappy's old directory: a leftover src/glitchygames/bitmappy/ (ignored __pycache__ ) resolves as a namespace package and fails test_the_old_engine_package_is_gone ; rm -rf src/glitchygames/bitmappy . The same applies to src/glitchygames/examples and tests/examples : ignored leftovers of the move ( __pycache__ ) make glitchygames.examples resolve as a namespace package in an editable install, and test_the_old_example_module_is_gone (in each moved member) and test_the_engines_examples_directory_is_gone fail. Their messages name the leftover locations; the remedy is rm -rf src/glitchygames/examples tests/examples . A member's console script resolves through its installed distribution: the golden plugin cannot find it unless --all-packages installed the member.
docs.title: Games as Their Own Packages

docs.text: A GlitchyGames game, demo or app can live in its own package beside the engine: a uv workspace member under src/ , depending on glitchygames like any third-party game would. This page explains what a member is, how to work with one, and how to move a game out of the engine into one. The why and the order of the moves are in the plan, plans/2026-10-24-workspace-packages.md .
docs.title: Games as Their Own Packages

docs.text: Four layers, all under src/ : src/ glitchygames/ the engine (distribution glitchygames); it has no examples package: every game and demo is a member, and its resources/ holds only what the engine itself ships games/<game>/ one member per game: every game (mr-muncher, clockwork-keep, brave-adventurer, paddleslap, drawing-fire) demos/<demo>/ one member per demo (dt-demo, joystick-demo, text-input-demo): a small program that shows one engine feature (console scripts `dt-demo`, `joystick-demo`, `text-input-demo`; no browser build) apps/<app>/ one member per application (Bitmappy) tests/ the engine's own tests scripts/ tools Nothing at the repository root is importable as one of our packages. Tests and tools run from the root import the installed engine and members ( uv sync installs them editable, nox non-editable), and tests/test_suite_collection.py checks that import glitchygames resolves to the installed package. Coverage maps the installed copies back to src/ ( [tool.coverage.paths] ), so its report names the files in the repository.
docs.title: The layout

docs.text: A demo (a demos-layer member): a program under src/demos/<demo>/ , run with its console script or python -m <package> . It is code. A game's bundled demo recording : <package>/demos/<name>.jsonl.gz , package data inside a game (PaddleSlap's rally.jsonl.gz ), replayed by that game's console script. It is data, and glitchygames.bundled_demos finds it (see "Bundled demos" below). A demos directory inside a package is therefore never a demos-layer member, and a demos-layer member's recordings (it has none today) would still be that member's own package data.
docs.title: Two meanings of "demo"

docs.text: A member is a directory under its layer, named after its distribution (with hyphens), holding: src/games/<game>/ pyproject.toml its metadata (below) README.md one paragraph: what it is, how to play and test it src/<package>/ its import package (underscores: a hyphen cannot be imported), never at the member's root, so nothing in the member directory can be imported by accident in place of the installed package tests/ its tests (no __init__.py), with its golden replay in tests/fixtures/replays/golden.jsonl.gz Its pyproject.toml follows Mr. Muncher's ( src/games/mr-muncher/pyproject.toml ): [project] name = "<distribution>" version = "1.0.0" description = "<one line>" requires-python = ">=3.14,<4.0" dependencies = [ "glitchygames" ] [project.scripts] < console-script > = "<package>:main" [build-system] requires = [ "hatchling" ] build-backend = "hatchling.build" [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages = [ "src/<package>" ] [tool.uv.sources] glitchygames = { workspace = true } A member that reuses another member's code depends on it too ( dependencies = ["glitchygames", "<other>"] , <other> = { workspace = true } ). Files inside the import package (a sprite TOML, a bundled demo) ship as package data: read them through the module's own path ( Path(__file__).parent / 'sprites' ), never through the repository.
docs.title: What a member is

docs.text: From the repository root: uv sync --all-extras --all-groups --all-packages # the engine and every member, with the dev tools uv run <console-script> # play it uv run pytest --no-cov src/games/<game>/tests # its tests alone (no coverage gate on a subset) uv run pytest # everything: the engine's and every member's tests A plain uv sync keeps every member installed (each is in the root's dev dependency group), but drops the dev tools: use the full command above. The 100% coverage gate covers the engine and every member together, so it is met only by the whole run. Each layer is also an extra of the engine, naming that layer's members, so an installer picks the engine alone or with them: uv build --all-packages # every wheel, into dist/ # (nox -s build-wheel does the same) pip install --find-links dist glitchygames # the engine pip install --find-links dist "glitchygames[games]" # the engine and every game pip install --find-links dist "glitchygames[demos,apps]" # the engine, the demos and the apps The names are not yet on PyPI (neither glitchygames nor any game's), so install from the built wheels as above: a plain pip install glitchygames would fetch whatever package someone else published under that name. ( uv sync --extra games does the same in the repository.) A layer with no member yet is an empty extra; tests/test_workspace_config.py keeps each extra equal to its layer's members. Recordings name games by logical names : <layer>.<module path inside the package>:<class> ( games.mr_muncher.game:MrMuncherScene ). A recording therefore does not depend on where the code lives, and moving a game changes no recording. The layers are data in the engine, src/glitchygames/logical_names.py : MEMBER_LAYERS for members (kept equal to the workspace by tests/test_workspace_config.py ). Every game, demo and Bitmappy is a member; the engine has no examples package. Golden replays live with the member's tests; the golden plugin collects them from every member, so the engine's uv run pytest replays each one. The browser build ships a member's package as its own archive ( <package>.zip ) beside the engine's glitchygames.zip ( scripts/build_browser_bundle.py , GameSpecification.member_packages ). API reference : scripts/gen_ref_pages.py writes a page per member package ( <package>/index.md ), listed under "Games API Reference" in mkdocs.yml , or under "Apps API Reference" for an app (Bitmappy's bitmappy/index.md ). Wheels : nox -s build-wheel builds the wheel of the engine and of every member ( uv build --all-packages ).
docs.title: Working with a member

docs.text: Historical: every game and demo has moved out and src/glitchygames/examples/ is gone (Part 3, 2026-10-26). A new game or demo starts as a fresh member. These steps record how the moves were done. The recipe Mr. Muncher's move followed ( plans/2026-10-24-workspace-packages-1-foundation.md , Task 9). Do one game per commit series, and verify each before the next. Every step names the check that fails if it is skipped: tests/test_workspace_config.py catches a member left out of any tool's configuration.
docs.title: Moving a game out of the engine

docs.text: git mv src/glitchygames/examples/<package> src/games/<game>/src/<package> , then delete what is left of the old directory: its git-ignored __pycache__ would otherwise keep an importable namespace package there. git mv of a directory carries its untracked __pycache__ along too: delete it in the member as well (its .pyc files name the old module). Move its tests to src/games/<game>/tests/ with no __init__.py (a tests directory must not be a package named tests : tests/test_suite_collection.py ). pytest imports every test module under its path from the repository root, never its bare file name ( src.games.mr-muncher.tests.test_mr_muncher_maze_and_actors , the same under uv run pytest and nox: --import-mode=importlib without namespace packages, the root on the path, in the root pyproject.toml ), so two members may have test files or helpers of the same name (BUGS.md #224 item 31). To patch a test module's own names, use __name__ ( mocker.patch(f'{__name__}.LOG') ). Name test files after the package by convention, test_<package>_<area>.py (Drawing Fire's test_drawing_fire_battle.py ). A helper module beside the tests is imported by that same path ( from src.apps.bitmappy.tests.film_strip_support import ... ), never by its bare name: tests/test_suite_collection.py::test_no_member_test_imports_a_module_by_a_bare_name fails on one. A member directory whose name holds a dash cannot be named in an import statement: give such a member's shared helpers to its tests as conftest.py fixtures (the simplest), or load one with importlib.import_module('src.games.mr-muncher.tests.maze_support') . A member may have a tests/conftest.py (Drawing Fire's drains the event queue). It is imported by its path too, so nothing may import conftest by name: look a conftest up as pytest registered it, by its path ( pytestconfig.pluginmanager.get_plugin(str(pytestconfig.rootpath / 'conftest.py')) ). Move its golden replay to src/games/<game>/tests/fixtures/replays/golden.jsonl.gz , its bytes unchanged. Data its tests read beside them (golden sounds, for instance) moves with them. Delete the emptied tests/fixtures/replays/<console-script>/ (and any parent it leaves empty: Drawing Fire's move emptied the root's tests/fixtures/ ). Rewrite glitchygames.examples.<package> imports to <package> ( git grep -l across the repository, excluding plans/ ), then read the whole diff: a docstring or a path string can match too.
docs.title: 1. Move the code and tests

docs.text: src/games/<game>/pyproject.toml (above) and README.md . The package's __init__.py re-exports main . The move's tests, one file per subject, each named test_<distribution with - as _>_<subject>.py ( tests/test_suite_collection.py refuses a test file named for anything else, or a name used twice). A member has only the subjects it has tests for: _logical_names.py : the game's classes keep the logical names its recordings hold (every member has this one); _install_location.py : the package imports from <member>/src/ (or site-packages in a wheel install), and (for a member that was once an example) importlib.util.find_spec('glitchygames.examples') is None, so a leftover ignored directory fails a test. A brand-new member, never an example, has no "old example module is gone" test; _wheel.py : the member's wheel holds only its package, plus its data (sprites, demos, resources); _package_data.py : the member's shipped data (a sprite library, a bundled demo) is inside the package, checked without building a wheel ( _wheel.py is for the tests that build one); _entry_points.py : the console script and python -m <package> resolve to main ; _recording_history.py : the golden's old path maps to its new one in the root pyproject.toml 's [tool.glitchygames] recording-renames (its history follows it), and so does every other moved recording. That is six subjects: logical_names, install_location, wheel, package_data, entry_points, recording_history. A move test outside them goes beside the member's other tests, named for its subject (Brave Adventurer's tests/core/test_brave_adventurer_shared_core.py , for example).
docs.title: 2. Create the member

docs.text: File What to add or change pyproject.toml Remove its console script from [project.scripts] (the member's own pyproject.toml has it now). Add the member to its layer's extra ( games , demos or apps in [project.optional-dependencies] ), [tool.uv.workspace] members , [tool.uv.sources] , the dev dependency group, pytest testpaths , addopts ( --cov=<package> ), coverage source and [tool.coverage.paths] , ruff src , include and namespace-packages (its tests), isort known-first-party , ty root and src.include , deptry known_first_party . Re-key any per-file ruff ignore that names the old path. pyrightconfig.json Add it to include , a tests environment (before the member's own) and the member's environment, each with the extraPaths Mr. Muncher's have. Every member is a src layout, so the environments name the member's src/ ( WorkspaceMember.import_roots in scripts/workspace_packages.py ), as Brave Adventurer's do: that is the one form. tests/test_workspace_config.py::test_every_member_keeps_its_packages_under_src enforces the layout, and no configuration entry may name a member path the workspace does not derive noxfile.py _CODE_DIRS , _SOURCE_PACKAGE_DIRS , _MEMBER_DISTRIBUTIONS wily.cfg The path list mkdocs.yml The mkdocstrings paths , and its API page under "Games API Reference" uv.lock Regenerate: uv lock
docs.title: 3. Register it in the root configuration

docs.text: src/glitchygames/logical_names.py : add its package to MEMBER_LAYERS . Its recordings need nothing else (their logical names do not change); tests/test_logical_names.py pins both tables. The root pyproject.toml 's [tool.glitchygames.recording-renames] : one line per moved recording, old path to new, so its run-ledger history stays connected. Each lookup is one step: a recording that has already moved once needs a line from each of its old paths.
docs.title: 4. Update the engine's tables

docs.text: The recording tools are the engine's, and the game has them without declaring anything ( --record-golden-trace , --record-session , --verify , --measure , ..., or glitchygames <tool> : Tools for any game ). What this repository adds is test data and its own tables: scripts/golden_inputs.py : the game's golden input script ( <package>_script ) and controls tail ( <package>_controls ), each a callable taking no arguments that returns an InputScript , importing what it reads of its game inside the function. Any tool reaches them as MODULE:NAME from the repository root ( --input-script scripts.golden_inputs:<package>_script , --controls-tail scripts.golden_inputs:<package>_controls ). scripts/record_golden_traces.py : add a '<module>:<class>' reference to GAME_SCENES (never a module-level import of a member: the subprocess import test fails on one), GAME_MODULES (whose value is the bare package name) and its input script's builder to SCRIPT_BUILDERS . It records on the engine's golden-trace harness ( glitchygames.replay.tools.golden_traces ). scripts/record_scripted_session.py records the golden replay on the engine's scripted-session recorder ( glitchygames.replay.tools.scripted_sessions , the record-session tool). Add the game's controls tail to CONTROLS_TAIL_BUILDERS , and the game to INPUT_ONLY_PLACEMENT_GAMES or POLLED_INPUT_GAMES when its script needs it. It derives its fixture directories from GAME_MODULES and the workspace ( REPLAY_FIXTURE_DIRECTORIES ), and refuses a game no member holds; edit its docstring's commands too. The root pyproject.toml 's [tool.glitchygames] games : add the member's console script, so glitchygames verify and glitchygames measure with no --game take its recordings. tests/replay/test_golden_replays.py : its imports, GAMEPLAY_ACTION_MAPS , ENGINE_SCENE_CONTROLS , UNEXERCISED_CONTROLS and any table naming the game. Engine tests no longer borrow a game, by import or by path: tests/test_suite_collection.py ( engine_test_imports_of_members ) fails on any root test that imports a member. Each kind of test lives in one place: The game's own tests are in the member ( src/games/<game>/tests/ ): its rules, sprites, touch controls, replays and the move's tests above. A test that only the game's code can answer goes there, not in tests/ . Engine tests use stand-ins : tests/stand_in_harness_games.py (games for the replay and harness tests) and tests/stand_in_games.py (games and distributions for the discovery, replay-plugin and playback tests). A test that needs a game, a root-layout example or several console scripts writes or imports a stand-in; it never imports a member. Cross-member tests discover through the workspace ( scripts/workspace_packages.py ) and assert hand-written expectations in tests/workspace_expectations.py ( EXPECTED_GOLDENS , EXPECTED_GAME_CONSOLE_SCRIPTS , EXPECTED_ALL_CONSOLE_SCRIPTS , EXPECTED_BUNDLED_DEMOS ). They are written out on purpose, because an expectation derived from the thing it checks checks nothing. Edit them when a game, golden, bundled demo or console script is added or removed. Also add the game to the control tables in tests/replay/golden_replay_controls.py , and to tests/replay/test_record_scripted_session.py::test_a_member_games_fixture_is_directly_in_the_members_replay_fixtures . The exemptions ( MEMBER_IMPORT_EXEMPT_MODULES and MEMBER_IMPORT_EXEMPT_NAMES in tests/test_suite_collection.py , each with its reason; a stale one fails): the module tests/replay/golden_replay_controls.py , whose per-game control tables are cross-member infrastructure moved there unchanged, and the eleven named imports in tests/world/test_golden_traces.py , whose per-game world rules measure the games' own drawings and players. Nothing else in tests/ may import a member. Every game is a member now (Drawing Fire, the last in the engine's examples, moved), so no game is a root-layout example any more. The root's fixtures/replays/<console-script>/ layout stays only as the replay plugin's layout for other projects; the tests of it ( tests/replay/test_replay_plugin.py , tests/replay/test_golden_replays.py , tests/test_code_tree.py , tests/test_measure_staged_replays.py ) use stand-ins: a tmp_path path, a stand-in installed distribution, a pytester copy. A new game or demo starts as a member; a test that needs a root-layout or several-console-script example writes one. Paths built with / ( ... / 'fixtures' / 'replays' / '<game>' / ... ) escape the grep below: also grep for '<console-script>' / and / '<console-script>' . git grep for the old package path and the old golden path across the repository: engine tests that borrow a game (a collision test using its sprites), benchmarks reading its golden, scripts importing it. Point each at the member, or move the test into the member when it is really the game's. Once done, the only matches left are on purpose: git grep -n \ "glitchygames.examples.<package>\|fixtures/replays/<game>" \ -- ':!plans' ':!quality' ':!BUGS.md' (grep's . matches any character, so the dotted pattern finds the slashed path too) prints only the recording-renames line (the old path is its point) and the member's move tests (the history check on that line in _recording_history.py , the old-package check and docstring in _install_location.py ). plans/ , quality/ (ledger rows) and BUGS.md are history and keep the old paths.
docs.title: 5. Update the scripts and tests that name it

docs.text: In scripts/build_browser_bundle.py , its GAMES entry's module becomes <package>.game and member_packages names its package (a tuple, dependencies first); its TOUCH_LAYOUTS entry is unchanged. tests/test_build_browser_bundle.py pins which games ship member packages. A game that depends on another member lists both, the one depended on first: each ships as its own archive.
docs.title: 6. The browser build

docs.text: docs/games/<game>.md : its file table and every path ( src/games/<game>/src/<package>/... ), and an "Its package" line linking here. docs/glitchygames/examples/index.md : remove its ::: block, if it has one (its API page is now generated from the member). README.md and CLAUDE.md : where the game lives.
docs.title: 7. The docs

docs.text: uv lock # then read its diff: only the new member uv sync --all-extras --all-groups --all-packages uv run --extra dev nox -s format-code lint-code lint-dependencies uv run basedpyright && uv run nox -s static-analysis-ty # The member's tests, its golden replay among them (no -k: a golden's id is # <console-script>/golden, hyphenated, so -k <package> would deselect it) uv run pytest --dummy-only --no-cov -q src/games/<game>/tests # The engine's checks on its golden replay, and its golden trace uv run pytest --dummy-only --no-cov -q \ tests/replay/test_golden_replays.py tests/world/test_golden_traces.py -k <package> # The configuration guards, and every engine test that borrows the game (step 5's git grep) uv run pytest --dummy-only --no-cov -q tests/test_suite_collection.py \ tests/test_workspace_config.py tests/test_workspace_packages.py tests/test_logical_names.py \ tests/test_browser_touch_controls.py tests/test_build_browser_bundle.py \ tests/engine/test_engine_lifecycle.py tests/test_recording_metrics.py \ tests/test_our_measured_recordings.py tests/test_measure_staged_replays.py \ tests/test_generate_performance_graphs.py tests/replay tests/world <borrowing tests> uv run pytest # the whole suite, both drivers, 100% coverage uv run <console-script> --verify # its golden replay and bundled demos, replayed headless uv run glitchygames unmeasured --game <console-script> # what --measure would measure of it uv build --package <distribution> # the member builds on its own uv run python -m scripts.build_browser_bundle <console-script> --output <scratch directory> uv run nox -s browser -- <console-script> # its browser bundle, served and opened uv run nox -s lint-docs # the docs build strictly The bundle built without serving must list <package>.zip in its pyscript.toml , and the member's wheel hold only its package. Before the whole suite, a coverage run of the member's tests and its borrowing tests ( --cov=<package> --cov-fail-under=0 ) shows its code still at 100% from where it now is. The golden replay is not re-recorded: its bytes are unchanged, and it replays strictly from its new place. Its first frame records the scene's module, so its content hash changes: glitchygames report shows that this is the only difference.
docs.title: 8. Verify

docs.text: The replay-metrics pre-commit hook ( scripts/measure_staged_replays.py , which runs glitchygames unmeasured , then glitchygames measure --code-tree TREE --rows-directory DIR ) measures every recording on the new code and stages the rows (about 12 s). It refuses a commit with untracked files under src/ or a partial commit, so stage the whole move ( git add -A src tests scripts docs ) before committing.
docs.title: 9. Commit

docs.text: A member that was never in a layer (Bitmappy, an app that lived in the engine as glitchygames.bitmappy , outside examples/ , so no layer table named it): its logical name changes when it moves, from its module path ( glitchygames.bitmappy.editor:BitmapEditorScene ) to apps.bitmappy.editor:BitmapEditorScene , so a recording made before the move no longer matches. A plain replay refuses such a recording, naming the remedy, and --replay-trace OLD --rebaseline NEW --headless converts it (a rebaseline compares the game and each scene by qualified name alone and writes the current logical names: gameplay replay ). A game that was already in a layer keeps its logical name when it moves, as the recipe above says. Bitmappy has no golden replay, so its move converted none; it keeps its tests named test_bitmappy_*.py , its sprite library as package data ( bitmappy.SPRITE_CONFIG_DIR ), and its member declares everything it imports itself (the engine's pyproject.toml no longer lists tenacity, for instance). Several games in one project (Brave Adventurer and its Egyptian edition, Papyrus): one member, built and published together, with layered import packages in its own src layout ( src/games/brave-adventurer/src/ ): the primitives both games share ( brave_adventurer_core ), each game on top of them ( brave_adventurer , brave_adventurer_papyrus ), and a launcher ( brave_adventurer_modes ) as the member's one console script. The launcher starts the game a recording's header names, so the golden-replay plugin's one console script per member replays every game's golden; the goldens are named apart ( golden-<game>.jsonl.gz ). A member that keeps several console scripts instead has each recording replayed through the one whose entry point's module holds the game its header names ( src/glitchygames/replay/tools/children.py , recorded_games_console_script ). scripts/record_scripted_session.py names each such game's golden ( GOLDEN_FIXTURE_NAMES ) and keys its console scripts by game ( GAME_CONSOLE_SCRIPTS ), as tests/replay/test_golden_replays.py keys each golden's controls: one script can replay several games' goldens. Share only by mechanical moves: recordings and golden traces name sprites by class name and creation order, so a class may change module but not name, and nothing may be created in a different order. Its browser bundle lists every archive a game needs, the shared ones first. A game that is one module (PaddleSlap's paddleslap.py ): its recordings name games.paddleslap:Game , so Game must stay defined in the package itself ( src/paddleslap/__init__.py ), not in a paddleslap/game.py it re-exports: a re-export does not change Game.__module__ , and the logical name would become games.paddleslap.game:Game . Ruff's non-empty-init-module (RUF067) is ignored for that file in pyproject.toml . A package's __init__ never runs as __main__ , so the module's if __name__ == '__main__' moves to src/<package>/__main__.py ( python -m paddleslap , as it was when the game lived in the engine's examples package). Bundled demos ship inside the package as package data, <package>/demos/<name>.jsonl.gz (PaddleSlap's paddleslap/demos/rally.jsonl.gz , read through Path(__file__).parent ). The engine finds them in the installed packages: glitchygames.bundled_demos.bundled_demos() ( find_spec over the packages its caller names, with no default; bookmarked copies left out) returns BundledDemo records (console script, installed path, install name). It is the one lookup: the replay plugin's bundled_demo_paths (which raises for a demo no console script replays) and glitchygames.replay.tools.recordings.game_recordings (a game's own demos, which --verify and --measure take) both call it. Development installs are editable ( uv sync , and the replay-metrics nox session's uv run --all-packages ), so the demos are found in the repository and the ledger names them by repository path; under a built install ( site-packages , as nox's test sessions install on purpose) a recording outside the repository is named by its install name ( glitchygames.replay.tools.measure.recording_ledger_name ). A demo moved twice needs a recording-renames line from each old path. Engine-private names : a member uses only the engine's public API. Where a game reaches into the engine, give the engine a public read-only API first, then move the game. PaddleSlap needed no private name once the engine offered BallSprite.trajectory and record_trajectory_point . A known exemption, member tests : a member's tests may use the engine's test seams (for example SceneManager._reset and FontManager._font_cache , which reset engine state between tests); the member's game code may not. A public testing helper for them is a follow-up ( plans/future-features.md , item #56).
docs.title: Special cases

docs.text: A plain uv sync drops the dev tools (pytest among them): use uv sync --all-extras --all-groups --all-packages . A member-only test run fails the coverage gate: add --no-cov , and let the whole run check coverage. An old example directory left on disk (its ignored __pycache__ ) is importable and shadows the member, and tests/test_suite_collection.py rejects a glitchygames/ directory at the root. Delete leftovers after moving. The same trap applies to Bitmappy's old directory: a leftover src/glitchygames/bitmappy/ (ignored __pycache__ ) resolves as a namespace package and fails test_the_old_engine_package_is_gone ; rm -rf src/glitchygames/bitmappy . The same applies to src/glitchygames/examples and tests/examples : ignored leftovers of the move ( __pycache__ ) make glitchygames.examples resolve as a namespace package in an editable install, and test_the_old_example_module_is_gone (in each moved member) and test_the_engines_examples_directory_is_gone fail. Their messages name the leftover locations; the remedy is rm -rf src/glitchygames/examples tests/examples . A member's console script resolves through its installed distribution: the golden plugin cannot find it unless --all-packages installed the member.
docs.title: Pitfalls

docs.text: Gameplay Recording and Replay # GlitchyGames can record a play session and replay it exactly through the real engine. Same engine version and same recording give bit-identical sprite traces: every frame's sprite rect and visible match the recording. Audio is played during a replay but is not compared. This page covers recording, exact replay, watching a replay (with step back and bookmarks), headless runs, the determinism audit, golden replays and rebaselining them, the tools any game gets (as its own flags and as the glitchygames command), in-game playback (demos, instant replay, ghosts), and the rules game code follows so its sessions replay. See plans/2026-10-19-gameplay-replay.md for the design and plans/future-work.md for the follow-ups. For how it works (a frame's steps and doors, speeds and timing, the file's fields, stored versus derived, and how playback is tested), see the overview, Gameplay Playback ; this page is the command reference. Quick start # # Record a session uv run paddleslap --record-trace session.jsonl.gz # Watch it replay exactly, comparing every frame with the recording (press Space to start) uv run paddleslap --replay-trace session.jsonl.gz # The same with no window, no sound and no pacing; the report goes to stdout, and the exit # code says whether it matched (0) or diverged (1) uv run paddleslap --replay-trace session.jsonl.gz --headless # Check that it replays the same way twice, in fresh processes with different hash seeds uv run paddleslap --replay-trace session.jsonl.gz --audit # After an intentional change: replay the same inputs on the current code, write what it does # to a new recording and print what changed uv run paddleslap --replay-trace session.jsonl.gz --rebaseline new-session.jsonl.gz --headless # Did the code get slower? Compare this machine's processing time per frame with the # recording's; with a limit, more than 10% slower exits 8 uv run paddleslap --replay-trace session.jsonl.gz --headless --max-processing-slowdown 10 # Onion skin: watch a replay with another recording's items drawn over it, half transparent uv run paddleslap --replay-trace new-session.jsonl.gz --compare-trace session.jsonl.gz # Play live against a recording: its items drawn over your game, half transparent uv run paddleslap --compare-trace session.jsonl.gz # The same tools as the glitchygames command (the game comes from the recording), and a # recording's runs, speed changes and behavior changes uv run glitchygames replay-trace session.jsonl.gz --headless uv run glitchygames report session.jsonl.gz Every flag above is one of the engine's tools, which every game has without declaring anything; Tools for any game lists them all. The doors # The engine takes everything from the outside world through a small set of doors , and game code reaches them only through the engine. Live play plugs live providers into the doors; replay plugs in providers that serve the recording. The game cannot tell which one it is talking to, so a replay runs the real engine and the real game code again. Door Live ( LiveSources ) Replay ( ReplaySources ) Event pump pygame's queue recorded batch N for pump call N Frame time the measured start-to-start time the recorded dt Polled input captured from pygame once per frame the recorded snapshot Devices real joysticks and controllers stand-ins built from the recording Saves files on disk ( DiskSaveManager ) in memory ( MemorySaveManager ), seeded from the recording Wall clock the real time the recording's start time plus the frame clock Random seed --random-seed or 64 random bits the recorded seed Pacing the target FPS the target FPS; none under --headless The modules: src/glitchygames/sources.py : the EngineSources protocol and the registry ( active_sources() , install_sources(sources=...) , reset_sources() ) and the frame clock. It is a leaf module with no engine imports, which avoids an import cycle between the engine and the scenes. install_sources is allowed only before the first frame, so a run never mixes live and recorded input. src/glitchygames/live_sources.py : LiveSources . src/glitchygames/recording.py : RecordingSources , which wraps the live doors under --record-trace and records what passes through them. src/glitchygames/replay/driver.py : ReplaySources , the comparison and the divergence report. tests/test_engine_doors.py scans the package and fails if any file but src/glitchygames/clock.py uses the time module (a read, time.sleep , anything) or reads datetime 's now, or if anything outside the doors polls pygame's keyboard or mouse, reads or posts pygame events directly, uses pygame's timers, or enumerates or opens joysticks and controllers. Its ALLOWED_BYPASSES lists the few exceptions, each with its reason. The engine's own pacing, measurement and diagnostics read real time through the clock module's raw functions ( raw_counter_ns() , raw_counter_seconds() , raw_sleep() , raw_wall_clock_time() ), which are never replayed and are not for game code. Rules for game code # Time # Read time from src/glitchygames/clock.py or Scene.game_time , never from time , datetime or pygame.time . Import the module and call through it ( from glitchygames import clock , then clock.elapsed_seconds() ), never a function by name: it is the one clock, so one patch on glitchygames.clock reaches every reader (the doors guard checks it): Use For Scene.game_time gameplay timers and cooldowns; stops while the scene is paused frame_clock_seconds() , frame_clock_milliseconds() blinks, animation, "how long since" in UI; never pauses wall_clock_time() , wall_clock_epoch_seconds() timestamps (save metadata, undo history, logs) elapsed_seconds() throttles, debounces, repeat intervals, timeouts (subtract two readings) measured_seconds() real durations for logs and metrics only elapsed_seconds() is the frame clock, live and in a replay, so a throttle near its threshold decides the same way both times; such timers advance once per frame. In a recorded run (and its replay) wall_clock_time() is the recording's start time ( recorded_at ) plus the frame clock, so a timestamp the game shows replays exactly; live play without recording reads the real wall clock. measured_seconds() is real monotonic time and is never replayed: never let its value change what is drawn, played or recorded. Text-widget cursor blinks use the frame clock, not Scene.game_time . A paused scene's widgets are neither updated nor drawn, so a blink cannot be seen advancing while the game is paused. Polled input # Read held keys, modifiers, the mouse and device positions from the frame's input snapshot, never from pygame: from glitchygames.input.state import current_input snapshot = current_input () # or GameEngine.input snapshot . key_pressed ( pygame . K_LEFT ) # by key code (follows the layout) snapshot . scancode_pressed ( scancode = pygame . KSCAN_W ) # by physical position (every layout) snapshot . modifiers # KMOD bits snapshot . mouse_position # (x, y) snapshot . mouse_buttons # (left, middle, right) snapshot . axis ( device_id = instance_id , axis = 0 ) # joystick layer, -1.0 .. 1.0 snapshot . button ( device_id = instance_id , button = 3 ) snapshot . hat ( device_id = instance_id , hat = 0 ) snapshot . controller_axis ( device_id = instance_id , axis = pygame . CONTROLLER_AXIS_LEFTX ) # int scale snapshot . controller_button ( device_id = instance_id , button = pygame . CONTROLLER_BUTTON_A ) The snapshot is immutable and is taken once per frame, right after the frame's first event pump. dt_tick runs before the pump, so there it is the previous frame's snapshot (the same lag as polling pygame had). Devices are keyed by instance id. A game controller is read on two layers: its joystick view ( axis , button , hat ) and the controller layer ( controller_axis , controller_button ). Held keys are physical positions (scancodes), and a key code depends on the keyboard layout (the key in the A position is K_q on AZERTY). A recording therefore also holds the key codes the held keys had on the recording machine, and a replay answers key_pressed(pygame.K_q) as that machine did, whatever the replaying machine's layout. Only pygame's K_* key codes are recorded. Limitation (BUGS.md #83): keys a layout adds that pygame names no K_* constant for, such as French é , German ß or Spanish ñ (SDL gives them their character's code point as the key code), are not in that list. The recorder can only find the held key codes by trying every K_* constant (pygame lets Python ask a key code's position, not a position's key code), so a game that polls one, say key_pressed(ord('é')) , reads it held live but not held in a replay, even on the machine that recorded it. Key events are unaffected (a recorded KEYDOWN or KEYUP keeps its key , whatever its value), and so are positional controls ( scancode_pressed , ActionMap.bind(scancode=...) ). Handle such keys through events or by position, not by polling their key code. For positional controls (movement, say), poll scancode_pressed(scancode=pygame.KSCAN_*) : no keymap is consulted, so it is the same key on every layout, live or replayed, as ActionMap.bind(scancode=...) is for events. Devices # Enumerate and open joysticks and controllers only through active_sources().devices() ( src/glitchygames/input/devices.py ): joystick_count() , controller_count() , is_controller(device_index=...) , name_for_index(device_index=...) , open_joystick(device_index=...) , open_controller(device_index=...) and joystick_for_instance(instance_id=...) . A recording stores every answer (failures included) and a descriptor of every opened device. A replay gives the recorded answers and stand-ins ( ReplayJoystick , ReplayController ) whose positions come from the snapshot and whose rumble is dropped, so it never needs the recorded hardware and never sees a device that happens to be plugged in. Saves # Open a save store with glitchygames.state.open_saves(app_name=...) . Live play gets a DiskSaveManager . A replay gets a MemorySaveManager seeded from the recording's snapshot of that namespace: reads see what the original session saw, writes stay in memory, and real saves are never touched. Both are SaveManager s, which hold every rule of the save format. A recording's header holds each store as it was first opened, so a first scene whose setup() writes to its saves (adds one to a play count) replays from the saves it found. Slots saved at the same time are listed by name, so list_slots() gives the same order everywhere. Events and randomness # Post events with glitchygames.recording.post_event , not pygame.event.post , so a recording can mark them internal. Replay delivers internal events from the code that posts them again; an SDL-type event posted directly would be delivered twice. Code that drives the game from outside its logic, as a player would (a supervisor, a test harness, a tool), posts with glitchygames.recording.post_input_event instead. The event is recorded as external input, whatever its type, so --replay-trace , instant replays and demos serve it whether or not they run the poster again (a copy the replayed code posts is dropped). A supervisor that posts with post_event is taken for the game itself, and a replay that does not run it diverges. While a demo or instant replay plays, its input posts of SDL types (keys, buttons, device and window events) are the player's input: a press ends a demo, a release is held for the live game, exactly as a replay of the session without the supervisor serves them. A supervisor may post any event this way, game events ( GAMEEVENT , MENUEVENT , any pygame.event.custom_type() ) included. The rule: input of an SDL type posted during a demo or instant replay counts as the player's; everything else reaches the game (after the demo or instant replay, if one is playing), live and replayed alike. Draw random numbers from the seeded named streams in src/glitchygames/randomness.py ( random_stream('name') , numpy_stream('name') ), never from the global random functions, secrets or an unseeded numpy generator. The supervisor hook and control events # A supervisor ( src/glitchygames/supervision.py ) is called once per frame at a fixed place: after logic and events, before frame services, camera aim and positioning. What it changes is drawn that frame and seen by collision on the next one. scene_manager . add_supervisor ( supervisor = my_supervisor ) # my_supervisor.on_frame(frame_number=..., scene=...) scene_manager . add_control_event_handler ( kind = 'breakpoint' , handler = on_breakpoint ) scene_manager . record_control_event ( kind = 'breakpoint' , data = { 'label' : 'ball through paddle' }) A control event is a supervisor action recorded in the frame it happened in. A replay applies the recorded control events again at the same frame's supervisor slot, so sessions with supervisor actions replay exactly. A future cheat device will use this hook and channel. Recording ( --record-trace PATH ) # A recording is a gzip JSON Lines trace (format version 3; versions 2 and 3 can be read): a header line, then exactly one line per main-loop frame. Each frame holds its dt , every event batch the engine read from SDL's queue (each event tagged external or internal ) and the sprites. Format 3 adds per-frame input_changes , control_events , devices_opened , saves_opened , device_enumeration and scene_start (each written only when not empty). The header holds the game, scene and versions, every option, the start time, the random seed, and the saves and devices the run took in before recording started. The full format is described in the src/glitchygames/recording.py module docstring. Scene starts # A recording also holds how each scene began, so in-game playback (demos, instant replay) can rebuild a scene from its start: the scene's first logic frame (the first frame whose dt_tick runs on it) carries its scene_start (its class's module and qualified name, so two loaded scenes of the same name are told apart, replay_arguments() , every random stream's state and the frame clock as its __init__ began and again as its first setup() began, the saves as they were before its __init__ ran, and the state its first logic frame began in; src/glitchygames/scene_start.py ). A playback starts there. Frame 0 holds the first scene's start when the run was started with --record-trace (or --rebaseline ). Starts are captured only while they can be used (recording, playback, or a scene that opts into instant replay), so live play pays nothing. A scene that cannot be rebuilt on its own sets CAPTURES_SCENE_START = False (the pause screen does). A replay never compares starts. A scene built with arguments besides options (Clockwork Keep's next floor carries the score and lives) returns them from replay_arguments() , as they were when it was built; they must read back from JSON exactly as returned: class FloorScene ( Scene ): def __init__ ( self , floor_index = 0 , player_score = 0 , options = None , groups = None ): super () . __init__ ( options = options , groups = groups ) # first: the start capture begins here self . floor_index = floor_index self . starting_player_score = player_score def replay_arguments ( self ): return { 'floor_index' : self . floor_index , 'player_score' : self . starting_player_score } Draw random numbers only after super().__init__() : the capture begins there. Replay ( --replay-trace PATH ) # At startup the replay reads the recording, applies its recorded options and seeds the random streams with its seed. It refuses, logging the reason and exiting with one of the exit codes , when: the recording is of another game (the header's game and each scene start's scene name their classes by logical names, src/glitchygames/logical_names.py : the layer, the module path inside the game's package, then : and the qualified name, as in games.mr_muncher.game:MrMuncherScene , which stay the same when the game's code moves; a recording made before logical names is compared by its exact game_module and scene_module , and a --rebaseline of it writes the logical names), cannot be read (not gzip, no permission, a directory) or has an unsupported format version: UNUSABLE_INPUT (65); the recording's game or scene has the same class name as the one loaded but another logical module (any class that moved to another logical module, for instance Bitmappy's scene, which left glitchygames.bitmappy.editor for apps.bitmappy.editor:BitmapEditorScene ): a plain replay cannot tell a moved class from a different class of that name, so it refuses with UNUSABLE_INPUT (65) and a message naming the remedy, --replay-trace OLD --rebaseline NEW --headless ( REBASELINE_REMEDY in src/glitchygames/replay/driver.py ). A --rebaseline compares such records by qualified name alone ( modules_not_compared , used for the game by check_recorded_game and for each scene start by find_scene_class in src/glitchygames/replay/playback.py ), and NEW holds the current logical names; the file does not exist: MISSING_INPUT (66); --record-trace is given too: OPTIONS_REFUSED (64). Recording over a replay is what --rebaseline does, and only it; its window does not open at the recorded display size: UNUSABLE_INPUT (65), with one line naming both sizes ( Cannot replay PATH: it was recorded on a 800x600 display, but the window opened at 800x480 (the window manager chose another size); refusing to replay it ). Games read the display's size (PaddleSlap places its paddles at half the screen height), so the replay opens its window at the size the recorded display had (the header's screen_size ), not at the recorded --resolution : a window manager may have given the recorded window another size than it asked for. A headless replay always gets that size; a watched one gets it unless the window manager refuses, and then the replay is refused as above. A recording whose header holds no screen_size (the engine's recorder always writes one; a hand-made header may not) replays at its recorded --resolution with a warning. A window resized during the recorded run is not recorded, so a game that reads the live size every frame can still diverge. A recording made by a different engine version replays with one warning. A version-2 recording replays with one warning too: it has no input snapshots, so polled input reads as idle. Each frame, the replay serves the recorded events, dt , input, devices, saves and clocks. Then it compares the frame with the recording: the active scene's class, then each recorded sprite in draw order (present, rect , visible ), along with the frame's internal events, control events and pump count. The first difference stops a headless replay, as does the last recorded frame; a watched replay pauses there instead. Closing the window stops any replay. Then it reports how it went (logged, or printed to stdout under --headless ). A sprite divergence lists that sprite in the last 20 frames up to the divergent one, as recorded and as replayed: Replay diverged at frame 6120: sprite Ball#2 rect expected [412, 300, 16, 16], got [412, 301, 16, 16] Ball#2, last 20 frames (expected | got): 6100: [400, 290, 16, 16] visible | [400, 290, 16, 16] visible ... 6120: [412, 300, 16, 16] visible | [412, 301, 16, 16] visible Other divergences (the scene, an event, the frame or pump count) are reported on their one line. A replay that matched reports Replay matched 9800 frames (end of recording) (or (quit before the end) , when the window was closed or a watched replay's viewer pressed Esc), and one that matched up to the cut-off of a truncated recording Replay ended early at frame 4312: the recording is truncated . Every replay that ends normally, watched or headless, exits with its result: SUCCESS (0) when it matched or was quit before the end, REPLAY_DIVERGED (1) when it diverged, UNUSABLE_INPUT (65) for a truncated recording. A crash, Ctrl-C, a signal or the game's own exit ends the run as for any run, and the report then says only where the replay stopped ( Replay stopped at frame 12: the run ended with INTERNAL_ERROR (70) ); if the replay had already reached its result, the report gives it, then then the run ended with ... (see exit codes ). The game's own successful exit ( sys.exit(0) ) before the replay reached its result exits REPLAY_DIVERGED (1), never SUCCESS , which would say it matched (a rebaseline takes it as the game ending early instead: below). A recording whose header or first frame cannot be decoded (a malformed device, saves or input field) is refused as unusable ( UNUSABLE_INPUT , 65), like an unreadable file. While a replay runs, real keyboard, mouse, touch, joystick, controller, device and window events are blocked at SDL, so they never reach the game (a watched replay leaves key presses and releases unblocked for its controls, which never pass them on to the game). The block is applied again on every pump (event managers created mid-run allow their types again). Each type's earlier blocked state is restored exactly when the replay ends, normally or after an error. QUIT, the window's close event and custom event types are never blocked, so closing the window still ends the replay. Blocking also refuses posts of those types: game code that fakes input by posting KEYDOWN loses the post, which shows up as a missing internal event divergence. A watched replay leaves KEYDOWN and KEYUP unblocked, so such a post arrives there and matches its recording: a recording of a game that posts keys can match watched and diverge headless (and under --audit ). Recorded window references in events are served as None , as live events of the display window carry. Watching a replay # A replay without --headless is watched: a read-only game inside a game ( src/glitchygames/replay/viewer.py ). The outer loop, the replay viewer, owns the window: it ticks 60 times a second of real time whatever the speed and whether paused, reads the viewer's keys, and presents the recorded game's latest frame with the status bar drawn on it. The inner loop, the recorded game, runs its frames in full (logic, update and render) at their recorded frame times: each tick runs as many as the real time since the last tick, times the speed, pays for (at most MAX_INNER_FRAMES_PER_TICK , and only within an 11 ms real-time budget per tick, so keys and drawing keep their 60 Hz). It never owes more than one tick's worth: after a stall it runs one bounded burst and drops the rest, and when the recorded game cannot keep up with the speed the status bar says so and shows the real speed ( can't keep up: ×3.2 ). So 1x shows about one recorded frame per tick, 8x about eight, ¼x one every fourth tick. Which frames run when never changes what they do, so a watched replay is exactly as exact as a headless one. It first runs frame 0, then holds on a start screen: that frame dimmed, "Press Spacebar to Start Game Replay" centred, and a smaller line naming the debug overlay's keys ( F3: debug overlay F4: next panel ). Frame 0's sounds play before Space, and a one-frame recording reaches its end at the start screen. The screen is drawn by the pause screen's MessageScreen ( src/glitchygames/ui/message_screen.py ) with its own message and look, as an overlay on the presented frame: switching to a real pause scene would change the recorded scene sequence. Nothing runs while the replay is held: no frame, no frame clock, no recorded input. The viewer's keys go to the replay's controls ( src/glitchygames/replay/controls.py ), never to the game. Each key acts once per press (the key repeat games turn on is ignored); . and , held act once, then after 300 ms ten times a second: Key Action Space Start the replay from the start screen, then pause or resume . While paused, run one frame , While paused, step back one frame (held: one more frame back per repeat, restarting once on release) Home Restart at the beginning, paused after frame 0 D Restart just before the divergence, once the replay has found one ] / [ Double or halve the playback speed (0.25 to 8) B Bookmark the frame shown in the status bar S Save a copy of the recording with the bookmarks as breakpoints Esc Quit the replay F3 / F4 Toggle the debug overlay / show its next panel A status bar at the bottom centre shows frame 6120 / 9800 · 1:42.0 · ×1 · paused · diverged at 6120 (the parts that apply), drawn on the presented frame after the debug overlay, so it is never in a screenshot or a trace. At a divergence or the end of the recording the replay pauses with the debug overlay on and a banner above the status bar ( Diverged at frame 6120: ... or End of recording ); stepping past the end does nothing, and Esc ends the run with the replay's result. Step back, Home and D # A replay cannot run backwards, and the engine cannot be rebuilt in-process, so these keys restart the replay in a fresh process ( src/glitchygames/replay/rebuild.py ) with the same command line (every option kept, --replay-fps included) plus --replay-pause-at-frame N , an explicit --debug-overlay or --no-debug-overlay , and the viewer's speed, debug panel and the divergence found so far ( --replay-viewer-state , internal; D works at once after a restart). The window closes and a new one opens; the end-of-run performance reports wait for the last replay.
