docs.text: Runs tweens simultaneously in parallel. All tweens update together each frame. The group is complete when every tween in it has finished. Parameters: tweens ( Tween [ object ] , default: () ) – The tweens to run in parallel. Source code in src/glitchygames/effects/tween.py 252 253 254 255 256 257 258 259 260 261 262 263 264 265 266 267 268 269 270 271 272 273 274 275 276 277 278 279 280 281 282 283 284 285 286 287 288 289 290 291 292 293 294 295 296 297 298 299 300 301 302 303 304 305 class TweenGroup : """Runs tweens simultaneously in parallel. All tweens update together each frame. The group is complete when every tween in it has finished. Args: tweens: The tweens to run in parallel. """ def __init__ ( self , * tweens : Tween [ object ]) -> None : """Initialize the group with tweens to run in parallel.""" self . _tweens : list [ Tween [ object ]] = list ( tweens ) self . _is_complete : bool = len ( self . _tweens ) == 0 def update ( self , dt : float ) -> bool : """Update all tweens in the group simultaneously. Args: dt: Delta time in seconds. Returns: True when all tweens in the group have completed. """ if self . _is_complete : return True all_done = True for tween in self . _tweens : if tween . is_active and not tween . update ( dt ): all_done = False if all_done : self . _is_complete = True return self . _is_complete def cancel ( self ) -> None : """Cancel all tweens in the group.""" for tween in self . _tweens : tween . cancel () self . _is_complete = True @property def is_complete ( self ) -> bool : """Whether all tweens in the group have finished.""" return self . _is_complete @property def is_active ( self ) -> bool : """Whether the group is still running.""" return not self . _is_complete

docs.text: Runs tweens one after another in sequence. Each tween starts only after the previous one completes. The sequence is complete when the last tween finishes. """ def __init__ ( self , * tweens : Tween [ object ]) -> None : """Initialize the sequence with tweens to run serially.""" self . _tweens : list [ Tween [ object ]] = list ( tweens ) self . _current_index : int = 0 self . _is_complete : bool = len ( self . _tweens ) == 0 def update ( self , dt : float ) -> bool : """Advance the current tween in the sequence. """ if self . _is_complete : return True current_tween = self . _tweens [ self . _current_index ] if current_tween . update ( dt ): self . _current_index += 1 if self . _current_index >= len ( self . _tweens ): self . _is_complete = True return True return False def cancel ( self ) -> None : """Cancel all tweens in the sequence.""" for tween in self . _tweens : tween . cancel () self . _is_complete = True @property def is_complete ( self ) -> bool : """Whether all tweens in the sequence have finished.""" return self . _is_complete @property def is_active ( self ) -> bool : """Whether the sequence is still running.""" return not self . _is_complete

Same value as # Python's os.EX_USAGE (sysexits.h EX_USAGE) OPTIONS_REFUSED = 64 # The recording or input data is unusable. Same value as Python's os.EX_DATAERR (sysexits.h # EX_DATAERR) UNUSABLE_INPUT = 65 # The input file does not exist. Same value as Python's os.EX_NOINPUT (sysexits.h EX_NOINPUT) MISSING_INPUT = 66 # A required service (the API server) cannot be reached. Same value as Python's # os.EX_UNAVAILABLE (sysexits.h EX_UNAVAILABLE) SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE = 69 # An uncaught exception during a run, or an audit that could not run. Same value as Python's # os.EX_SOFTWARE (sysexits.h EX_SOFTWARE) INTERNAL_ERROR = 70 # An output file or directory cannot be created or written. Same value as Python's # os.EX_CANTCREAT (sysexits.h EX_CANTCREAT) CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT = 73 # Stopped by SIGHUP (Unix only): 128 + signal.SIGHUP HANGUP = 129 # Stopped by SIGINT (Ctrl-C): 128 + signal.SIGINT INTERRUPTED = 130 # Stopped by SIGTERM: 128 + signal.SIGTERM TERMINATED = 143 # Stopped by SIGBREAK (Windows only: Ctrl-Break): 128 + signal.SIGBREAK BREAK = 149 @classmethod def for_signal ( cls , signal_number : int ) -> ExitCode : """Return the member a run stopped by a signal exits with. Args: signal_number: The signal (``signal.SIGTERM`` and so on). Returns: ``HANGUP``, ``INTERRUPTED``, ``TERMINATED`` or ``BREAK``. Raises: ValueError: For a signal the engine does not wire (see the module docstring), rather than a number with no name. """ message = f 'signal { signal_number } has no exit code: the engine does not handle it' if signal_number <= 0 : raise ValueError ( message ) try : return cls ( SIGNAL_EXIT_STATUS_BASE + signal_number ) except ValueError as error : raise ValueError ( message ) from error def describe ( self ) -> str : """Return the code's name and number, as logs show it. ``str()`` of an IntEnum member is only its number (Python 3.11 on). Returns: For example ``'OPTIONS_REFUSED (64)'``. """ return f ' { self . name } ( { self . value } )' @classmethod def describe_status ( cls , status : int ) -> str : """Describe any process exit status: a member, a signal exit, or an unknown number. Args: status: A process's exit status (a child's ``returncode``). Returns: ``'INTERNAL_ERROR (70)'`` for a member; for a signal, ``'signal 6 (134)'`` (128 + the signal number, as a shell reports it) or, for a process killed by the signal (a subprocess reports -N), ``'TERMINATED (signal 15)'`` where the signal has a member and ``'signal 6'`` otherwise; any other number alone. """ if status < 0 : signal_number = - status try : return f ' { cls . for_signal ( signal_number ) . name } (signal { signal_number } )' except ValueError : return f 'signal { signal_number } ' try : return cls ( status ) . describe () except ValueError : pass if status > SIGNAL_EXIT_STATUS_BASE : return f 'signal { status - SIGNAL_EXIT_STATUS_BASE } ( { status } )' return str ( status )

Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 3540 3541 3542 3543 3544 3545 3546 3547 3548 3549 3550 3551 3552 3553 3554 3555 3556 3557 3558 3559 3560 3561 3562 3563 3564 3565 3566 3567 3568 3569 3570 3571 3572 3573 3574 def handle_event ( self , event : events . HashableEvent ) -> None : """Handle pygame events. Args: event (pygame.event.Event): The event to handle. """ # First check for system-level QUIT event (window close button) if event . type == pygame . QUIT : self . log . info ( 'Window close requested' ) self . scene_manager . quit_requested = True return # Check if there are any focused sprites in the current scene scene = self . scene_manager . active_scene if scene and scene . all_sprites : focused_sprites = [ sprite for sprite in scene . all_sprites if hasattr ( sprite , 'is_active' ) and sprite . is_active ] # If we have focused sprites, ALL key events go to the scene if focused_sprites and event . type == pygame . KEYDOWN : self . scene_manager . handle_event ( event ) return # Only handle engine-level key events if no focused sprites if event . type == pygame . KEYDOWN and getattr ( event , 'key' , None ) == pygame . K_q : self . log . info ( 'Quit key pressed with no focused sprites' ) self . scene_manager . quit_requested = True return # Pass other events to the scene manager self . scene_manager . handle_event ( event )

docs.text: Initialize the game arguments. A game argument with a flag the engine already added (a tool's, --force , or a general one, --resolution ) is refused before anything runs: the process exits ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED with a message naming the flag ( reserved_flag_refusal ), not argparse's traceback. Parameters: game ( type [ Scene ] | Scene ) – The game instance. Returns: options ( dict [ str , Any ] ) – The game arguments. Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 1064 1065 1066 1067 1068 1069 1070 1071 1072 1073 1074 1075 1076 1077 1078 1079 1080 1081 1082 1083 1084 1085 1086 1087 1088 1089 1090 1091 1092 1093 1094 1095 1096 1097 1098 1099 1100 1101 1102 1103 1104 1105 1106 1107 1108 1109 1110 1111 1112 1113 1114 1115 1116 1117 1118 1119 1120 1121 1122 1123 1124 1125 1126 1127 1128 1129 1130 1131 @classmethod def initialize_arguments ( cls , game : type [ Scene ] | Scene ) -> dict [ str , Any ]: """Initialize the game arguments. A game argument with a flag the engine already added (a tool's, ``--force``, or a general one, ``--resolution``) is refused before anything runs: the process exits ``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED`` with a message naming the flag (``reserved_flag_refusal``), not argparse's traceback. Args: game: The game instance. Returns: options (dict[str, Any]): The game arguments. """ parser : argparse . ArgumentParser = argparse . ArgumentParser ( f ' { game . NAME } version { game . VERSION } ' , ) parser = GameEngine . args ( parser ) # args is a class method, which allows us to call it before initializing a game # object, which allows us to query all of the game engine objects for their # command line parameters. It is optional (Scene does not declare it): looked up by name game_args_method : Callable [ ... , Any ] | None = getattr ( game , 'args' , None ) if game_args_method is not None : try : game_args_method ( parser . add_argument_group ( f ' { game . NAME } v { game . VERSION } Options' )) except argparse . ArgumentError as error : # Every game has the engine's flags, so a clash fails every run of the game, not # only a tool's: said as a usage error, with the engine's code for one parser . exit ( status = ExitCode . OPTIONS_REFUSED , message = ( f ' { parser . prog } : error: ' f ' { reserved_flag_refusal ( game_name = game . NAME , error = error ) } \n ' ), ) args : argparse . Namespace = parser . parse_args () # Set the logging level logging . basicConfig ( format = LOG_FORMAT , level = args . log_level . upper (), ) if game_args_method is None : # A hint for the game's author, at INFO (--log-level info shows it). Logged once the # level is set: before basicConfig only Python's last-resort handler saw it, which # drops INFO, so it never showed at any level (D18's report) cls . log . info ( 'Game does not implement arguments. Add a def args(parser) class method.' ) GameEngine . OPTIONS = vars ( args ) # type: ignore[reportConstantRedefinition] # Resolve the effective target FPS; --target-fps defaults to None so that an explicit # value (including 0 = uncapped) can be told apart from "not passed". GameEngine . OPTIONS [ 'target_fps' ] = cls . resolve_target_fps ( command_line_target_fps = GameEngine . OPTIONS . get ( 'target_fps' ), game = game , ) options : dict [ str , Any ] = GameEngine . OPTIONS # Back propagate the options game . options = options return options

docs.text: Initialize the display. Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 1412 1413 1414 1415 1416 1417 1418 1419 1420 1421 1422 1423 1424 1425 1426 1427 1428 1429 1430 1431 1432 1433 1434 1435 1436 1437 1438 1439 1440 1441 1442 1443 1444 1445 1446 1447 1448 1449 1450 1451 1452 1453 def initialize_display ( self : Self ) -> None : """Initialize the display.""" # Let's try to set a resolution to the most compatible for # the system. If we don't provide any parameters, we'll get # a reasonble default, but you should consider whether that's # a good idea for your particular application. # # There are various caveats for hardware accelerated blitting # that make it undesirable in a lot of cases, so we'll just use # software. self . display_info = pygame . display . Info () self . initial_resolution : tuple [ int , int ] = ( self . display_info . current_w , self . display_info . current_h , ) self . cursor : list [ str ] = self . set_cursor ( cursor = None ) # Set the screen update type. if self . scene_manager . update_type == 'update' : self . display_update = pygame . display . update elif self . scene_manager . update_type == 'flip' : self . display_update = pygame . display . flip else : self . log . error ( 'Screen update type was neither "update" nor "flip".' ) # The Pygame documentation recommends against using hardware accelerated blitting. # # Note that you can also get the screen with pygame.display.get_surface() # # An existing window (a test's, or one a game opened first) may take its new size # only after set_mode returns (x11): the game is set up on the size it really has self . screen : pygame . Surface = set_display_mode ( size = self . desired_resolution , flags = self . mode_flags , ) # A new display is black, which cannot be told from "nothing rendered": until the # first scene draws, it shows the default background (glitchygames/backgrounds.py) paint_default_background ( surface = self . screen ) # A scene manager made before this display (pygame started first) holds the surface # of the display it saw then, which a --headless restart closed: it draws on this one self . scene_manager . screen = self . screen

docs.text: Initialize event handlers. The engine calls this on your behalf. Event subsystem bootstrapping This gives us much faster event processing than doing a lookup every time an event comes in since we can just call the processing function directly. It's not as fast as a raw pygame event loop, but since we layer richer event types on top of the pygame raw events, this gives us a nice balance of extensibility with performance. The engine calls this on your behalf. Event subsystem bootstrapping This gives us much faster event processing than doing a lookup every time an event comes in since we can just call the processing function directly. It's not as fast as a raw pygame event loop, but since we layer richer event types on top of the pygame raw events, this gives us a nice balance of extensibility with performance. """ for event_type in events . AUDIO_EVENTS : GameEngine . EVENT_HANDLERS [ event_type ] = self . process_audio_event for event_type in events . APP_EVENTS : GameEngine . EVENT_HANDLERS [ event_type ] = self . process_app_event for event_type in events . MIDI_EVENTS : GameEngine . EVENT_HANDLERS [ event_type ] = self . process_midi_event for event_type in events . WINDOW_EVENTS : GameEngine . EVENT_HANDLERS [ event_type ] = self . process_window_event for event_type in events . GAME_EVENTS : GameEngine . EVENT_HANDLERS [ event_type ] = self . process_game_event self . initialize_input_event_handlers () # Enable all events, except the window system's raw messages (SYSWMEVENT) unless the # game declares NATIVE_WINDOW_MESSAGES = True. # Note that glitchygames will auto-suppress events not handled # by the game once they are encountered, so it is recommended to enable all. events . allow_every_event_type ( native_window_messages = self . native_window_messages ( game = self . game ) )

docs.text: Process every event queued this frame. pygame.event.get() removes the whole batch from SDL's queue at once, so every event of the batch is handled here: none may be dropped. Each event is judged on its own; an event whose type has no entry in EVENT_HANDLERS , or whose handler did not handle it, goes to process_unimplemented_event . Parameters: should_discard ( Callable [[ Event ], bool ] | None , default: None ) – Returns True for an event to remove from the batch without processing it (not counted as unhandled). SceneManager passes is_discarded_during_transition during a transition. Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if at least one event was dispatched and every dispatched event was bool – handled (a raw-event scene's process_event counts as handled). False if any bool – dispatched event was unhandled, or if nothing was dispatched: an empty batch, or bool – one whose events were all discarded. Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 3576 3577 3578 3579 3580 3581 3582 3583 3584 3585 3586 3587 3588 3589 3590 3591 3592 3593 3594 3595 3596 3597 3598 3599 3600 3601 3602 3603 3604 3605 3606 3607 3608 3609 3610 3611 3612 3613 3614 3615 3616 3617 3618 3619 3620 3621 3622 3623 3624 3625 3626 3627 3628 3629 3630 def process_events ( self : Self , * , should_discard : Callable [[ pygame . event . Event ], bool ] | None = None ) -> bool : """Process every event queued this frame. ``pygame.event.get()`` removes the whole batch from SDL's queue at once, so every event of the batch is handled here: none may be dropped. Each event is judged on its own; an event whose type has no entry in ``EVENT_HANDLERS``, or whose handler did not handle it, goes to ``process_unimplemented_event``. Args: should_discard: Returns True for an event to remove from the batch without processing it (not counted as unhandled). SceneManager passes ``is_discarded_during_transition`` during a transition. Returns: bool: True if at least one event was dispatched and every dispatched event was handled (a raw-event scene's ``process_event`` counts as handled). False if any dispatched event was unhandled, or if nothing was dispatched: an empty batch, or one whose events were all discarded. """ raw_events = self . _pump_events () # Polled input is read once per frame, right after the pump, so it agrees with this # frame's events; it stays fixed until the next frame's pump, so dt_tick (which runs # before this) reads the previous frame's snapshot (glitchygames/input/state.py) set_current_input ( snapshot = active_sources () . input_snapshot ()) dispatched_event_count = 0 every_event_was_handled = True for pygame_event in raw_events : if should_discard is not None and should_discard ( pygame_event ): continue dispatched_event_count += 1 # Support scenes processing pygame raw events, bypassing # the glitchygames.engine event processing altogether if hasattr ( self . _active_scene , 'process_event' ): self . _active_scene . process_event ( pygame_event ) # type: ignore[union-attr] # ty: ignore[call-non-callable] continue event = events . HashableEvent . from_pygame ( pygame_event ) # Decided per event: a type missing from the map is unhandled event_was_handled = False if event . type in GameEngine . EVENT_HANDLERS : event_was_handled = bool ( GameEngine . EVENT_HANDLERS [ event . type ]( event )) # If an event is not in the event handler map, or the function # called didn't handle the event in question, we'll process it # as an unimplemented event if not event_was_handled : self . process_unimplemented_event ( event ) every_event_was_handled = False return dispatched_event_count > 0 and every_event_was_handled

docs.text: Resolve the effective target FPS. Order: explicit command line value (0 = uncapped) > the game's TARGET_FPS (when not None) > DEFAULT_TARGET_FPS. Parameters: command_line_target_fps ( float | None ) – The --target-fps value, or None if it was not passed. game ( type [ Scene ] | Scene ) – The game scene class or instance, which may declare TARGET_FPS. Returns: float ( float ) – The effective target FPS (0 means uncapped). Raises: TypeError – If the game's TARGET_FPS is neither None nor a (non-bool) number. ValueError – If the game's TARGET_FPS is negative, NaN or infinite. Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 1016 1017 1018 1019 1020 1021 1022 1023 1024 1025 1026 1027 1028 1029 1030 1031 1032 1033 1034 1035 1036 1037 1038 1039 1040 1041 1042 1043 1044 1045 1046 1047 1048 1049 1050 1051 1052 1053 1054 1055 1056 1057 1058 1059 1060 1061 1062 @staticmethod def resolve_target_fps ( * , command_line_target_fps : float | None , game : type [ Scene ] | Scene , ) -> float : """Resolve the effective target FPS. Order: explicit command line value (0 = uncapped) > the game's TARGET_FPS (when not None) > DEFAULT_TARGET_FPS. Args: command_line_target_fps: The --target-fps value, or None if it was not passed. game: The game scene class or instance, which may declare TARGET_FPS. Returns: float: The effective target FPS (0 means uncapped). Raises: TypeError: If the game's TARGET_FPS is neither None nor a (non-bool) number. ValueError: If the game's TARGET_FPS is negative, NaN or infinite. """ if command_line_target_fps is not None : return float ( command_line_target_fps ) # Looked up by name: TARGET_FPS is optional on a game (Scene does not declare it) game_target_fps = getattr ( game , 'TARGET_FPS' , None ) if game_target_fps is None : return DEFAULT_TARGET_FPS scene_class = game if isinstance ( game , type ) else type ( game ) # bool is a subclass of int, so it must be rejected explicitly. if isinstance ( game_target_fps , bool ) or not isinstance ( game_target_fps , ( int , float )): message = ( f ' { scene_class . __name__ } .TARGET_FPS must be a number or None, ' f 'got { game_target_fps !r} ' ) raise TypeError ( message ) if not math . isfinite ( game_target_fps ) or game_target_fps < 0 : message = ( f ' { scene_class . __name__ } .TARGET_FPS must be a finite number >= 0 ' f '(0 = uncapped), got { game_target_fps !r} ' ) raise ValueError ( message ) return float ( game_target_fps )

docs.text: Start the game engine. However the run ends, the teardown ( _shutdown : recordings closed) runs first; if the teardown itself raises, the run exits ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR (both errors logged). An exception raised before start(), in __init__ , is not mapped: it exits with Python's default 1 (each game has its own entry point, so there is no one place to wrap; see glitchygames/exit_codes.py). A replay ( --replay-trace ) that ends normally exits with its own code ( ReplayResult.exit_code under its exit policy), watched or headless. How it ends ( _begin_start and _crash_boundary raise these): RuntimeError if the game is not initialized; SystemExit with ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR after an uncaught exception (logged with its traceback), ExitCode.INTERRUPTED after Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt), or whatever status a SystemExit raised during the run carries (a signal handler's, a game's own), except a game's own successful exit that cuts a replay short ( ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED ; a rebaseline ends normally then, with what the game ran); at the normal end of a replay, with the replay's exit code ( ExitCode.SUCCESS , ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED or ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT for a truncated recording). Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 3034 3035 3036 3037 3038 3039 3040 3041 3042 3043 3044 3045 3046 3047 3048 3049 3050 3051 3052 3053 3054 3055 3056 def start ( self : Self ) -> None : """Start the game engine. However the run ends, the teardown (``_shutdown``: recordings closed) runs first; if the teardown itself raises, the run exits ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` (both errors logged). An exception raised before start(), in ``__init__``, is not mapped: it exits with Python's default 1 (each game has its own entry point, so there is no one place to wrap; see glitchygames/exit_codes.py). A replay (``--replay-trace``) that ends normally exits with its own code (``ReplayResult.exit_code`` under its exit policy), watched or headless. How it ends (``_begin_start`` and ``_crash_boundary`` raise these): RuntimeError if the game is not initialized; SystemExit with ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` after an uncaught exception (logged with its traceback), ``ExitCode.INTERRUPTED`` after Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt), or whatever status a SystemExit raised during the run carries (a signal handler's, a game's own), except a game's own successful exit that cuts a replay short (``ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED``; a rebaseline ends normally then, with what the game ran); at the normal end of a replay, with the replay's exit code (``ExitCode.SUCCESS``, ``ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED`` or ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` for a truncated recording). """ profiler = self . _begin_start () with self . _crash_boundary ( profiler = profiler ): self . _run_game ()

docs.text: Start the game engine, giving control back to the caller between frames. For a host that must not block (a browser: glitchygames/host.py). The run is start() 's, inside the same crash boundary (the same teardown and exit codes), but its frames are driven by one awaited wait_for_tick() per outer tick: a live game's by GameHost.run_async (an inner frame on the ticks TickPacer picks for the target FPS), a watched replay's by its viewer ( run_watched_replay_async : the tick's inner frames, then the viewer's outer frame). Parameters: wait_for_tick ( Callable [[], Awaitable [ float ]] ) – Waits for the next outer tick (a browser animation frame) and returns its timestamp in seconds. It ends as start() does (see there). Raises: RuntimeError – If the run is a headless replay (it never holds between frames, so it would never give control back), or (from _begin_start ) the game is not initialized. --compare-trace is refused before anything starts, exiting ( exit_with ) with ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED : OLD is replayed by a child process, which a browser page (the host start_async is for) cannot start ( _refuse_a_comparison_in_a_browser ). Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 3058 3059 3060 3061 3062 3063 3064 3065 3066 3067 3068 3069 3070 3071 3072 3073 3074 3075 3076 3077 3078 3079 3080 3081 3082 3083 3084 3085 3086 3087 3088 3089 3090 3091 3092 3093 3094 3095 3096 3097 3098 3099 3100 3101 3102 3103 3104 3105 3106 3107 3108 3109 3110 3111 3112 3113 async def start_async ( self : Self , * , wait_for_tick : Callable [[], Awaitable [ float ]]) -> None : """Start the game engine, giving control back to the caller between frames. For a host that must not block (a browser: glitchygames/host.py). The run is ``start()``'s, inside the same crash boundary (the same teardown and exit codes), but its frames are driven by one awaited ``wait_for_tick()`` per outer tick: a live game's by ``GameHost.run_async`` (an inner frame on the ticks ``TickPacer`` picks for the target FPS), a watched replay's by its viewer (``run_watched_replay_async``: the tick's inner frames, then the viewer's outer frame). Args: wait_for_tick: Waits for the next outer tick (a browser animation frame) and returns its timestamp in seconds. It ends as ``start()`` does (see there). Raises: RuntimeError: If the run is a headless replay (it never holds between frames, so it would never give control back), or (from ``_begin_start``) the game is not initialized. ``--compare-trace`` is refused before anything starts, exiting (``exit_with``) with ``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED``: OLD is replayed by a child process, which a browser page (the host start_async is for) cannot start (``_refuse_a_comparison_in_a_browser``). """ self . _refuse_a_comparison_in_a_browser () # Chosen first (a run start_async cannot drive is refused before anything starts), but # called inside the boundary run_frames : Callable [[], Awaitable [ None ]] if self . host is not None : run_frames = functools . partial ( self . host . run_async , scene_manager = self . scene_manager , wait_for_tick = wait_for_tick ) elif self . replay_sources is not None and not self . replay_sources . options . headless : run_frames = functools . partial ( run_watched_replay_async , scene_manager = self . scene_manager , viewer = self . replay_sources . viewer , wait_for_tick = wait_for_tick , ) else : raise RuntimeError ( ASYNC_RUN_NEEDS_HOST_MSG ) profiler = self . _begin_start () with self . _crash_boundary ( profiler = profiler ): if self . _begin_run (): if self . _power_on_plays (): self . _hand_back_power_on ( outcome = await play_power_on_async ( screen = self . screen , sources = active_sources (), wait_for_tick = wait_for_tick , ) ) self . _build_game ( paced_by_timer = False ) await run_frames ()
docs.title: start_async

docs.text: Start recording the session to a trace file (before the first frame). The header also holds what the run took in before recording started: a snapshot of every save store the doors opened ( saves ), the descriptors of devices opened ( devices ) and the enumeration answers given ( device_enumeration ). Then RecordingSources are installed around the active doors and record every frame from what passes through them (glitchygames/recording.py). SIGTERM (and SIGHUP on Unix, SIGBREAK on Windows) ends a started run through the normal teardown ( exit_on_signal , installed by start ), and so does SIGINT (KeyboardInterrupt). stop_trace_recording (called by _shutdown ) closes the file. Recording must start before the first frame: afterwards installing its doors raises SourcesAlreadyRunningError (from install_sources ; glitchygames/sources.py). Parameters: path ( Path ) – The recording's file. Returns: GameplayRecorder – The recorder. Raises: TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError – If this engine is already recording. Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 1949 1950 1951 1952 1953 1954 1955 1956 1957 1958 1959 1960 1961 1962 1963 1964 1965 1966 1967 1968 1969 1970 1971 1972 1973 1974 1975 1976 1977 1978 1979 1980 1981 1982 1983 1984 1985 1986 1987 1988 1989 1990 1991 1992 1993 1994 1995 1996 1997 1998 1999 2000 2001 2002 2003 2004 2005 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 def start_trace_recording ( self : Self , * , path : Path ) -> GameplayRecorder : """Start recording the session to a trace file (before the first frame). The header also holds what the run took in before recording started: a snapshot of every save store the doors opened (``saves``), the descriptors of devices opened (``devices``) and the enumeration answers given (``device_enumeration``). Then ``RecordingSources`` are installed around the active doors and record every frame from what passes through them (glitchygames/recording.py). SIGTERM (and SIGHUP on Unix, SIGBREAK on Windows) ends a started run through the normal teardown (``exit_on_signal``, installed by ``start``), and so does SIGINT (KeyboardInterrupt). ``stop_trace_recording`` (called by ``_shutdown``) closes the file. Recording must start before the first frame: afterwards installing its doors raises ``SourcesAlreadyRunningError`` (from ``install_sources``; glitchygames/sources.py). Args: path: The recording's file. Returns: The recorder. Raises: TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError: If this engine is already recording. """ if self . trace_recorder is not None : message = ( f 'start_trace_recording() was called while recording to ' f ' { self . trace_recorder . path } ; one run records once' ) raise TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError ( message ) inner = active_sources () registry = inner . devices () # A store a run started with --record-trace opened before recording started is in the # header as first opened: the first scene's setup() may have written to it since, and # the replay runs that setup() again (LiveSources.first_open_save_snapshots, read # through the host's doors in a hosted run) first_open_snapshots : Mapping [ str , dict [ str , Any ]] = ( inner . first_open_save_snapshots if isinstance ( inner , LiveSources | HostSources ) else {} ) # A rebaseline copies these fields from the replayed recording instead (rebaseline.py) header = { ** self . trace_recording_header (), SAVES_HEADER_FIELD : { namespace : ( first_open_snapshots [ namespace ] if namespace in first_open_snapshots else save_namespace_snapshot ( saves = store ) ) for namespace , store in inner . opened_save_namespaces . items () }, DEVICES_HEADER_FIELD : [ descriptor . to_json () for descriptor in registry . take_opened_descriptors () ], DEVICE_ENUMERATION_FIELD : [ answer . to_json () for answer in registry . take_enumeration_answers () ], } recorder = GameplayRecorder ( path = path , header = header ) install_sources ( sources = RecordingSources ( inner = inner , recorder = recorder )) self . trace_recorder = recorder self . log . info ( 'Recording gameplay to %s (random seed %s )' , path , self . random_seed ) return recorder
docs.title: start_trace_recording

The ``RecordingSources`` stay installed (the run is ending); with the recorder closed they only delegate. docs.text: Describe every unhandled event type, most frequent first. Each line names the type (pygame's event name and its number, so custom and unknown types still show), its count, when it was first seen and the first event's attribute names, e.g. JOYDEVICEADDED (1541) x1, first at 0.3 s, attributes: device_index, guid . Returns: list [ str ] – One line per type; empty when every event was handled. Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 4235 4236 4237 4238 4239 4240 4241 4242 4243 4244 4245 4246 4247 4248 4249 4250 4251 4252 4253 4254 4255 4256 def unhandled_event_report ( self : Self ) -> list [ str ]: """Describe every unhandled event type, most frequent first. Each line names the type (pygame's event name and its number, so custom and unknown types still show), its count, when it was first seen and the first event's attribute names, e.g. ``JOYDEVICEADDED (1541) x1, first at 0.3 s, attributes: device_index, guid``. Returns: One line per type; empty when every event was handled. """ records = sorted ( self . unhandled_events . items (), key = lambda item : item [ 1 ] . count , reverse = True , ) return [ f ' { pygame . event . event_name ( event_type ) . upper () } ( { event_type } ) x { record . count } , ' f 'first at { record . first_seen_seconds : .1f } s, ' f 'attributes: { ", " . join ( record . attribute_names ) or "none" } ' for event_type , record in records ]

docs.text: Get an attribute from the first proxy that has it. This method is called when an attribute is not found. Parameters: attr ( str ) – The attribute to get. Returns: Callable [..., Any ] – The attribute. Raises: AttributeError – If no proxy has the attribute (or there are no proxies yet). Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 421 422 423 424 425 426 427 428 429 430 431 432 433 434 435 436 437 438 439 440 441 442 443 444 445 446 447 448 449 450 def __getattr__ ( self : Self , attr : str ) -> Callable [ ... , Any ]: """Get an attribute from the first proxy that has it. This method is called when an attribute is not found. Args: attr: The attribute to get. Returns: The attribute. Raises: AttributeError: If no proxy has the attribute (or there are no proxies yet). """ # The proxies themselves are an instance attribute: before __init__ sets them there are # none to try (looking them up here would recurse) if attr == 'proxies' : raise AttributeError ( MISSING_ATTRIBUTE_MSG . format ( cls = type ( self ), attr = attr )) # Try each proxy in turn (BUGS.md #198: the lookup returned or raised on the first) for proxy in self . proxies : try : return getattr ( proxy , attr ) except AttributeError : continue if self . proxies : self . log . error ( 'No proxies for %s . %s ' , type ( self ), attr ) raise AttributeError ( NO_PROXIES_MSG . format ( cls = type ( self ), attr = attr ))

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 1425 1426 1427 1428 1429 1430 1431 1432 1433 1434 1435 1436 1437 1438 1439 1440 1441 1442 1443 1444 1445 1446 1447 1448 1449 1450 1451 1452 1453 1454 1455 1456 1457 1458 1459 1460 1461 1462 1463 1464 1465 1466 1467 1468 1469 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Return a path as the startup options block shows it. Inside the project, its stored path ( stored_path : relative to the root, POSIX-style); anywhere else absolute (the coordinator's ruling, 2026-10-28), where stored_path would keep only the file name, or a path in another checkout. Parameters: path ( str | PathLike [ str ] ) – The path as given. project_root ( Path | None ) – The project's root ( find_project_root ), or None. Returns: str – The path to show. Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 def displayed_path ( * , path : str | os . PathLike [ str ], project_root : Path | None ) -> str : """Return a path as the startup options block shows it. Inside the project, its stored path (``stored_path``: relative to the root, POSIX-style); anywhere else absolute (the coordinator's ruling, 2026-10-28), where ``stored_path`` would keep only the file name, or a path in another checkout. Args: path: The path as given. project_root: The project's root (``find_project_root``), or None. Returns: The path to show. """ resolved = Path ( path ) . expanduser () . resolve () if project_root is not None : stored = stored_path ( path = path , project_root = project_root ) # The stored path is shown only when it leads back to the path from this project's root if ( project_root . resolve () / stored ) . resolve () == resolved : return stored return str ( resolved )

docs.text: End the run with SystemExit, so GameEngine.start()'s teardown still runs. Installed by GameEngine.start for each of terminating_signals() that nothing else handles, for the whole run, so a recording is closed by _shutdown . It ignores further signals of the same kind before raising: a second SIGTERM ( uv run forwards one to its child as well, and pkill can match both) would otherwise raise again inside the teardown and leave the recording unclosed. _shutdown restores the default handling after closing the recording. It does nothing else: logging here could fail with "reentrant call" if the signal interrupted a write to the same stream. Parameters: signal_number ( int ) – The signal received. _frame ( FrameType | None ) – The interrupted frame (unused). Raises: SystemExit – Always, with ExitCode.for_signal(signal_number) ( TERMINATED for SIGTERM, HANGUP for SIGHUP, BREAK for SIGBREAK). Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 288 289 290 291 292 293 294 295 296 297 298 299 300 301 302 303 304 305 306 307 308 309 def exit_on_signal ( signal_number : int , _frame : FrameType | None ) -> None : """End the run with SystemExit, so GameEngine.start()'s teardown still runs. Installed by ``GameEngine.start`` for each of ``terminating_signals()`` that nothing else handles, for the whole run, so a recording is closed by ``_shutdown``. It ignores further signals of the same kind before raising: a second SIGTERM (``uv run`` forwards one to its child as well, and ``pkill`` can match both) would otherwise raise again inside the teardown and leave the recording unclosed. ``_shutdown`` restores the default handling after closing the recording. It does nothing else: logging here could fail with "reentrant call" if the signal interrupted a write to the same stream. Args: signal_number: The signal received. _frame: The interrupted frame (unused). Raises: SystemExit: Always, with ``ExitCode.for_signal(signal_number)`` (``TERMINATED`` for SIGTERM, ``HANGUP`` for SIGHUP, ``BREAK`` for SIGBREAK). """ signal . signal ( signal_number , signal . SIG_IGN ) raise SystemExit ( ExitCode . for_signal ( signal_number ))
docs.title: exit_on_signal

docs.text: Return how --list-input-devices prompts for a device, or None when it must not wait. It prompts only when stdin and stdout are a terminal: a person is there to plug a device in (or press Ctrl-C). A script, a pipe or CI gets the listing at once, never a wait. Returns: Callable [[ str ], None] | None – A writer of the prompt line (to stdout, flushed), or None. Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 440 441 442 443 444 445 446 447 448 449 450 451 452 453 454 455 456 457 def input_device_prompt () -> Callable [[ str ], None ] | None : """Return how --list-input-devices prompts for a device, or None when it must not wait. Returns: A writer of the prompt line (to stdout, flushed), or None. docs.text: Make each of terminating_signals() raise SystemExit, if nothing else handles it yet. The engine's one way of installing exit_on_signal ( GameEngine._install_signal_handlers for a run, run_inside_tool_crash_boundary for a tool on either front end). While it is installed, a SIGTERM (or SIGHUP, SIGBREAK) raises SystemExit wherever this process waits, so subprocess.run kills and reaps a child it is waiting for instead of leaving it running. Limitation: Python sets signal handlers from the main thread only. On another thread none is installed, and SDL's own handler is off (SDL_NO_SIGNAL_HANDLERS), so SIGTERM (or SIGHUP, SIGBREAK) then kills the process the system's default way, without the teardown: a recording is left unclosed (it still reads up to its last full frame). Returns: list [ int ] – The signals it installed the handler for ( restore_default_signal_handling puts them list [ int ] – back). Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 343 344 345 346 347 348 349 350 351 352 353 354 355 356 357 358 359 360 361 362 363 364 365 366 367 368 369 370 371 372 373 def install_exit_on_signal_handlers () -> list [ int ]: """Make each of terminating_signals() raise SystemExit, if nothing else handles it yet. The engine's one way of installing ``exit_on_signal`` (``GameEngine._install_signal_handlers`` for a run, ``run_inside_tool_crash_boundary`` for a tool on either front end). While it is installed, a SIGTERM (or SIGHUP, SIGBREAK) raises SystemExit wherever this process waits, so ``subprocess.run`` kills and reaps a child it is waiting for instead of leaving it running. Limitation: Python sets signal handlers from the main thread only. On another thread none is installed, and SDL's own handler is off (SDL_NO_SIGNAL_HANDLERS), so SIGTERM (or SIGHUP, SIGBREAK) then kills the process the system's default way, without the teardown: a recording is left unclosed (it still reads up to its last full frame). Returns: The signals it installed the handler for (``restore_default_signal_handling`` puts them back). """ installed : list [ int ] = [] for signal_number in terminating_signals (): try : # Limitation: a C-level handler (SDL's, when pygame was initialized before the # engine set SDL_NO_SIGNAL_HANDLERS) is invisible here, as getsignal still # reports SIG_DFL; installing then replaces it, which is what the engine wants if signal . getsignal ( signal_number ) == signal . SIG_DFL : signal . signal ( signal_number , exit_on_signal ) installed . append ( signal_number ) except ValueError as signal_error : # Signal handlers can only be set from the main thread LOG . debug ( 'Signal %d handler not installed: %s ' , signal_number , signal_error ) return installed
docs.title: install_exit_on_signal_handlers

docs.text: Return an options mapping's lines: sorted, name = value , aligned, nested indented. A name that suggests a secret ( is_secret_option_name ) shows REDACTED_OPTION_VALUE , whatever its value, at any depth. A non-empty mapping is shown below its name, one level deeper; any other value is pprint 's, its further lines (a long list) under the first. Parameters: options ( Mapping [ Any , Any ] ) – The options (or a mapping nested in one). indent ( str ) – The lines' indentation. Returns: list [ str ] – The lines, without line ends. Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 616 617 618 619 620 621 622 623 624 625 626 627 628 629 630 631 632 633 634 635 636 637 638 639 640 641 642 643 644 645 646 647 648 649 650 651 652 653 654 def options_block_lines ( * , options : Mapping [ Any , Any ], indent : str ) -> list [ str ]: """Return an options mapping's lines: sorted, ``name = value``, aligned, nested indented. A name that suggests a secret (``is_secret_option_name``) shows ``REDACTED_OPTION_VALUE``, whatever its value, at any depth. A non-empty mapping is shown below its name, one level deeper; any other value is ``pprint``'s, its further lines (a long list) under the first. Args: options: The options (or a mapping nested in one). indent: The lines' indentation. Returns: The lines, without line ends. """ names = sorted ( options , key = str ) width = max (( len ( str ( name )) for name in names ), default = 0 ) lines : list [ str ] = [] for name in names : value = options [ name ] prefix = f ' { indent }{ str ( name ) . ljust ( width ) } = ' if is_secret_option_name ( name = str ( name )): lines . append ( f ' { prefix }{ REDACTED_OPTION_VALUE } ' ) elif isinstance ( value , Mapping ) and value : lines . append ( prefix . rstrip ()) lines . extend ( options_block_lines ( options = cast ( 'Mapping[Any, Any]' , value ), indent = indent + OPTIONS_BLOCK_INDENT , ) ) else : # Any value at all (an empty mapping too): pformat writes each as Python would first , * rest = pprint . pformat ( cast ( 'object' , value ), width = max ( OPTIONS_BLOCK_WIDTH - len ( prefix ), 1 ) ) . splitlines () lines . append ( f ' { prefix }{ first } ' ) lines . extend ( f ' { " " * len ( prefix ) }{ line } ' for line in rest ) return lines

docs.text: Say which of a game's argument's flags the engine already has, and that it reserves them. argparse raises ArgumentError when the game's args adds an argument with a flag the engine's parser holds ( conflicting option string(s): --force ). Each conflicting flag is named: one of the engine's tools' ( registry.tool_flags : glitchygames --help lists them), or one of every game's general options (its --help lists them). Parameters: game_name ( str ) – The game's name ( NAME ). error ( ArgumentError ) – What argparse raised (its argument_name : the game's argument, all its flags). Returns: str – The message. Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 312 313 314 315 316 317 318 319 320 321 322 323 324 325 326 327 328 329 330 331 332 333 334 335 336 337 338 339 340 def reserved_flag_refusal ( * , game_name : str , error : argparse . ArgumentError ) -> str : """Say which of a game's argument's flags the engine already has, and that it reserves them. argparse raises ``ArgumentError`` when the game's ``args`` adds an argument with a flag the engine's parser holds (``conflicting option string(s): --force``). Each conflicting flag is named: one of the engine's tools' (``registry.tool_flags``: ``glitchygames --help`` lists them), or one of every game's general options (its ``--help`` lists them). Args: game_name: The game's name (``NAME``). error: What argparse raised (its ``argument_name``: the game's argument, all its flags). Returns: The message. """ # argparse's message is "conflicting option string(s): FLAG, FLAG" _ , _ , listed = error . message . partition ( ': ' ) flags_of_the_tools = tool_flags () reasons = [ f ' { flag } is reserved by the engine for its tools (glitchygames --help lists them)' if flag in flags_of_the_tools else f ' { flag } is reserved by the engine (an option of every game: --help lists them)' for flag in listed . split ( ', ' ) ] return ( f " { game_name } 's argument { error . argument_name } : { '; ' . join ( reasons ) } . Rename the game's " 'argument' )

docs.text: Run a tool inside the crash boundary and signal handling a game's run gets. The one boundary of both front ends' tools: a game flag's ( GameEngine._run_game_flag_tool ) and the glitchygames command's (glitchygames/replay/tools/command.py). While the tool runs, a terminating signal raises SystemExit with its own code ( exit_on_signal ), so a child the tool waits for is killed and reaped by subprocess.run before this process ends; the handlers are put back afterwards. However the tool ends is turned into an exit status, as start() 's run turns a run's ending into one ( _crash_boundary ): Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt): ExitCode.INTERRUPTED ( subprocess.run has stopped and reaped a child first, as for a signal); a recording write that failed part way: ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT ; any other exception: ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR , logged with its traceback as Runtime error during game execution @ tool '<tool>' , then report_hint (an ERROR line of its own) when there is one. A SystemExit (a signal handler's) passes through with its own code. Parameters: run_tool ( Callable [[], int ] ) – Runs the tool and returns its exit status. tool_description ( str ) – How the log names the tool (its flag: --verify ). report_hint ( str | None ) – What to do to report a crash ( BUG_REPORT_HINT , on a game, which takes --log-level ), or None (the glitchygames command, which has no such option). Returns: tuple [ int , BaseException | None] – The exit status, and the exception that ended the tool (None when it returned). Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 387 388 389 390 391 392 393 394 395 396 397 398 399 400 401 402 403 404 405 406 407 408 409 410 411 412 413 414 415 416 417 418 419 420 421 422 423 424 425 426 427 428 429 430 431 432 433 434 435 436 437 def run_inside_tool_crash_boundary ( * , run_tool : Callable [[], int ], tool_description : str , report_hint : str | None ) -> tuple [ int , BaseException | None ]: """Run a tool inside the crash boundary and signal handling a game's run gets. The one boundary of both front ends' tools: a game flag's (``GameEngine._run_game_flag_tool``) and the ``glitchygames`` command's (glitchygames/replay/tools/command.py). While the tool runs, a terminating signal raises SystemExit with its own code (``exit_on_signal``), so a child the tool waits for is killed and reaped by ``subprocess.run`` before this process ends; the handlers are put back afterwards. However the tool ends is turned into an exit status, as ``start()``'s run turns a run's ending into one (``_crash_boundary``): - Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt): ``ExitCode.INTERRUPTED`` (``subprocess.run`` has stopped and reaped a child first, as for a signal); - a recording write that failed part way: ``ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT``; - any other exception: ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR``, logged with its traceback as ``Runtime error during game execution @ tool '<tool>'``, then ``report_hint`` (an ERROR line of its own) when there is one. A SystemExit (a signal handler's) passes through with its own code. Args: run_tool: Runs the tool and returns its exit status. tool_description: How the log names the tool (its flag: ``--verify``). report_hint: What to do to report a crash (``BUG_REPORT_HINT``, on a game, which takes ``--log-level``), or None (the ``glitchygames`` command, which has no such option). Returns: The exit status, and the exception that ended the tool (None when it returned). """ installed = install_exit_on_signal_handlers () cause : BaseException | None = None try : exit_status = run_tool () except KeyboardInterrupt as interrupt : # Ctrl-C: never an internal error exit_status , cause = ExitCode . INTERRUPTED , interrupt except RecordingWriteError as error : # The disk filled part way: logged on one line by the recorder (BUGS.md #82) exit_status , cause = ExitCode . CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT , error except Exception as error : LOG . exception ( "Runtime error during game execution @ tool ' %s '" , tool_description ) if report_hint is not None : # Its own line after the traceback (logged above), where a player reads last LOG . error ( report_hint ) # ruff: ignore[error-instead-of-exception] exit_status , cause = ExitCode . INTERNAL_ERROR , error finally : # A signal's SystemExit (exit_on_signal) passes through with its own code restore_default_signal_handling ( signal_numbers = installed ) return exit_status , cause
docs.title: run_inside_tool_crash_boundary

This architecture reduces code footprint, and allows maxium flexibility when needed, at the expense of a bit of abstraction. Shared instances ( SHARES_INSTANCE , True for the event managers): a class has one instance, the first one constructed. Constructing it again returns that instance as it is, without running __init__ again (BUGS.md #198), so MouseEventManager() is the manager the GameEngine made to process mouse events with. Each engine run releases them ( release_shared_instances ) before it makes its managers, so a second engine in one process (a recording, then its replay) builds its own. A class that sets SHARES_INSTANCE = False gets a new instance at every construction: the proxies (a manager owns its own, and the controller manager one per controller) and EventManager ( GameEngine and SceneManager , whose own __new__ keeps its singleton). docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

Parameters: **changes ( object , default: {} ) – The fields to change or add; type may be given only unchanged. Returns: Self ( Self ) – The changed copy; this event is left as it was. Raises: TypeError – If changes gives the event another type. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 647 648 649 650 651 652 653 654 655 656 657 658 659 660 661 662 663 664 def with_fields ( self : Self , ** changes : object ) -> Self : """Return a copy of the event with some fields changed or added (the same class). Args: **changes: The fields to change or add; ``type`` may be given only unchanged. Returns: Self: The changed copy; this event is left as it was. Raises: TypeError: If ``changes`` gives the event another type. """ fields : dict [ str , object ] = { ** self . __dict__ , ** changes } new_type = fields . pop ( 'type' ) if new_type != self . type : raise TypeError ( EVENT_TYPE_CHANGE_MSG . format ( old = self . type , new = new_type )) return self . __class__ ( self . type , ** fields )

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 1425 1426 1427 1428 1429 1430 1431 1432 1433 1434 1435 1436 1437 1438 1439 1440 1441 1442 1443 1444 1445 1446 1447 1448 1449 1450 1451 1452 1453 1454 1455 1456 1457 1458 1459 1460 1461 1462 1463 1464 1465 1466 1467 1468 1469 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, with_fields ) computes its own. Returns: int ( int ) – The hash value. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 915 916 917 918 919 920 921 922 923 924 925 926 927 928 929 930 931 932 933 934 935 936 937 938 939 940 941 942 943 @override def __hash__ ( self : Self ) -> int : """Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, ``with_fields``) computes its own. Returns: int: The hash value. """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 1425 1426 1427 1428 1429 1430 1431 1432 1433 1434 1435 1436 1437 1438 1439 1440 1441 1442 1443 1444 1445 1446 1447 1448 1449 1450 1451 1452 1453 1454 1455 1456 1457 1458 1459 1460 1461 1462 1463 1464 1465 1466 1467 1468 1469 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 1425 1426 1427 1428 1429 1430 1431 1432 1433 1434 1435 1436 1437 1438 1439 1440 1441 1442 1443 1444 1445 1446 1447 1448 1449 1450 1451 1452 1453 1454 1455 1456 1457 1458 1459 1460 1461 1462 1463 1464 1465 1466 1467 1468 1469 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, with_fields ) computes its own. Returns: int ( int ) – The hash value. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 915 916 917 918 919 920 921 922 923 924 925 926 927 928 929 930 931 932 933 934 935 936 937 938 939 940 941 942 943 @override def __hash__ ( self : Self ) -> int : """Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, ``with_fields``) computes its own. Returns: int: The hash value. """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )
docs.title: __new__

docs.text: Set the state of the object. The event is rebuilt from the state's attributes exactly as init builds it, so it equals and hashes like the event the state came from (BUGS.md #121: this hashed a dict). The event is rebuilt from the state's attributes exactly as __init__ builds it, so it equals and hashes like the event the state came from (BUGS.md #121: this hashed a dict). The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. docs.text: Describe the event as JSON: {"type": <number>, "attributes": {...}} . docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )
