docs.text: Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, with_fields ) computes its own. Returns: int ( int ) – The hash value. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 915 916 917 918 919 920 921 922 923 924 925 926 927 928 929 930 931 932 933 934 935 936 937 938 939 940 941 942 943 @override def __hash__ ( self : Self ) -> int : """Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, ``with_fields``) computes its own. Returns: int: The hash value. """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, with_fields ) computes its own. Returns: int ( int ) – The hash value. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 915 916 917 918 919 920 921 922 923 924 925 926 927 928 929 930 931 932 933 934 935 936 937 938 939 940 941 942 943 @override def __hash__ ( self : Self ) -> int : """Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, ``with_fields``) computes its own. Returns: int: The hash value. """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Set the state of the object. The event is rebuilt from the state's attributes exactly as init builds it, so it equals and hashes like the event the state came from (BUGS.md #121: this hashed a dict). The event is rebuilt from the state's attributes exactly as __init__ builds it, so it equals and hashes like the event the state came from (BUGS.md #121: this hashed a dict). The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Parameters: pygame_event ( Event ) – The raw event. Returns: HashableEvent ( HashableEvent ) – The event. Event ) -> HashableEvent : """Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class (``EVENT_CLASSES``): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds (``HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict)``), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Args: pygame_event: The raw event. Returns: HashableEvent: The event. """ event_type = pygame_event . type event = object . __new__ ( EVENT_CLASSES . get ( event_type , HashableEvent )) fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = event_type fields . update ( pygame_event . dict ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) return event

Returns: int ( int ) – The hash value. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, ``with_fields``) computes its own. Returns: int: The hash value. """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, with_fields ) computes its own. Returns: int ( int ) – The hash value. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 915 916 917 918 919 920 921 922 923 924 925 926 927 928 929 930 931 932 933 934 935 936 937 938 939 940 941 942 943 @override def __hash__ ( self : Self ) -> int : """Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, ``with_fields``) computes its own. Returns: int: The hash value. """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Get an attribute from the first proxy that has it. This method is called when an attribute is not found. Parameters: attr ( str ) – The attribute to get. Returns: Callable [..., Any ] – The attribute. Raises: AttributeError – If no proxy has the attribute (or there are no proxies yet). Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 421 422 423 424 425 426 427 428 429 430 431 432 433 434 435 436 437 438 439 440 441 442 443 444 445 446 447 448 449 450 def __getattr__ ( self : Self , attr : str ) -> Callable [ ... , Any ]: """Get an attribute from the first proxy that has it. This method is called when an attribute is not found. Args: attr: The attribute to get. Returns: The attribute. Raises: AttributeError: If no proxy has the attribute (or there are no proxies yet). """ # The proxies themselves are an instance attribute: before __init__ sets them there are # none to try (looking them up here would recurse) if attr == 'proxies' : raise AttributeError ( MISSING_ATTRIBUTE_MSG . format ( cls = type ( self ), attr = attr )) # Try each proxy in turn (BUGS.md #198: the lookup returned or raised on the first) for proxy in self . proxies : try : return getattr ( proxy , attr ) except AttributeError : continue if self . proxies : self . log . error ( 'No proxies for %s . %s ' , type ( self ), attr ) raise AttributeError ( NO_PROXIES_MSG . format ( cls = type ( self ), attr = attr ))

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 1425 1426 1427 1428 1429 1430 1431 1432 1433 1434 1435 1436 1437 1438 1439 1440 1441 1442 1443 1444 1445 1446 1447 1448 1449 1450 1451 1452 1453 1454 1455 1456 1457 1458 1459 1460 1461 1462 1463 1464 1465 1466 1467 1468 1469 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented
docs.title: __subclasshook__

docs.text: Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, with_fields ) computes its own. Returns: int ( int ) – The hash value. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 915 916 917 918 919 920 921 922 923 924 925 926 927 928 929 930 931 932 933 934 935 936 937 938 939 940 941 942 943 @override def __hash__ ( self : Self ) -> int : """Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, ``with_fields``) computes its own. Returns: int: The hash value. """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class ( EVENT_CLASSES ): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Parameters: pygame_event ( Event ) – The raw event. Returns: HashableEvent ( HashableEvent ) – The event. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 619 620 621 622 623 624 625 626 627 628 629 630 631 632 633 634 635 636 637 638 639 640 @staticmethod def from_pygame ( pygame_event : pygame . event . Event ) -> HashableEvent : """Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class (``EVENT_CLASSES``): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds (``HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict)``), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Args: pygame_event: The raw event. Returns: HashableEvent: The event. """ event_type = pygame_event . type event = object . __new__ ( EVENT_CLASSES . get ( event_type , HashableEvent )) fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = event_type fields . update ( pygame_event . dict ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) return event

docs.text: Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, with_fields ) computes its own. Returns: int ( int ) – The hash value. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 915 916 917 918 919 920 921 922 923 924 925 926 927 928 929 930 931 932 933 934 935 936 937 938 939 940 941 942 943 @override def __hash__ ( self : Self ) -> int : """Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, ``with_fields``) computes its own. Returns: int: The hash value. """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 1049 1050 1051 1052 1053 1054 1055 1056 1057 1058 1059 1060 1061 1062 1063 1064 1065 def __setstate__ ( self : Self , state : builtins . dict [ str , Any ]) -> None : """Set the state of the object. The event is rebuilt from the state's attributes exactly as __init__ builds it, so it equals and hashes like the event the state came from (BUGS.md #121: this hashed a dict). """ attributes = dict ( state ) event_type = attributes . pop ( 'type' ) # A state pickled before BUGS.md #179 carries the hash it stored as an attribute attributes . pop ( '_HashableEvent__hash' , None ) self . __dict__ . clear () # Rebuilt as __new__ builds an event; the cached hash (none yet: pickle builds the # event just before) is cleared, so the event hashes by the state's content fields = self . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = event_type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , None )

docs.text: Build an event from to_json 's description (or a recording's event record). A recorded window reference (a recording's records hold them) becomes None, as a replay serves it. The class is the type's ( EVENT_CLASSES ), as for the constructor. A malformed record raises the recording's TraceFormatError ( glitchygames.recording.event_from_record ). Parameters: record ( Mapping [ str , JsonValue ] ) – {"type": <number>, "attributes": {...}} , as read back from JSON. Returns: Self ( Self ) – The event. A recorded window reference (a recording's records hold them) becomes None, as a replay serves it. The class is the type's (``EVENT_CLASSES``), as for the constructor. A malformed record raises the recording's ``TraceFormatError`` (``glitchygames.recording.event_from_record``). Args: record: ``{"type": <number>, "attributes": {...}}``, as read back from JSON. Returns: Self: The event. """ # Deferred: glitchygames.recording imports the sources and input modules, which import # the events package from glitchygames.recording import ( WINDOW_REFERENCE , RecordedReference , event_from_record , ) pygame_event = event_from_record ( dict ( record )) attributes = { name : ( None if isinstance ( value , RecordedReference ) and value . kind == WINDOW_REFERENCE else value ) for name , value in pygame_event . dict . items () } return cls ( pygame_event . type , ** attributes )

docs.text: Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class ( EVENT_CLASSES ): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Parameters: pygame_event ( Event ) – The raw event. Returns: HashableEvent ( HashableEvent ) – The event. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 619 620 621 622 623 624 625 626 627 628 629 630 631 632 633 634 635 636 637 638 639 640 @staticmethod def from_pygame ( pygame_event : pygame . event . Event ) -> HashableEvent : """Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class (``EVENT_CLASSES``): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds (``HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict)``), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Args: pygame_event: The raw event. Returns: HashableEvent: The event. """ event_type = pygame_event . type event = object . __new__ ( EVENT_CLASSES . get ( event_type , HashableEvent )) fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = event_type fields . update ( pygame_event . dict ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) return event

Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 647 648 649 650 651 652 653 654 655 656 657 658 659 660 661 662 663 664 def with_fields ( self : Self , ** changes : object ) -> Self : """Return a copy of the event with some fields changed or added (the same class). """ fields : dict [ str , object ] = { ** self . __dict__ , ** changes } new_type = fields . pop ( 'type' ) if new_type != self . type : raise TypeError ( EVENT_TYPE_CHANGE_MSG . format ( old = self . type , new = new_type )) return self . __class__ ( self . type , ** fields )

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 1425 1426 1427 1428 1429 1430 1431 1432 1433 1434 1435 1436 1437 1438 1439 1440 1441 1442 1443 1444 1445 1446 1447 1448 1449 1450 1451 1452 1453 1454 1455 1456 1457 1458 1459 1460 1461 1462 1463 1464 1465 1466 1467 1468 1469 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 1425 1426 1427 1428 1429 1430 1431 1432 1433 1434 1435 1436 1437 1438 1439 1440 1441 1442 1443 1444 1445 1446 1447 1448 1449 1450 1451 1452 1453 1454 1455 1456 1457 1458 1459 1460 1461 1462 1463 1464 1465 1466 1467 1468 1469 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Bases: UserDict [ str , Any ] Hashable, immutable event class. Hashable events are cacheable, so we can mitigate some of the performance overhead of glitchygames' event subsystem by caching events, which will result in an immediate return if an identical event is encountered, saving some function overhead and processing. Games are welcome to use the built-in pygame event subsystem, but on_*_event callbacks will not be available in that case. The class is chosen by the event's type: HashableEvent(pygame.MOUSEMOTION, ...) builds a MouseMotionEvent ( EVENT_CLASSES ), so every event of a type is an instance of that type's class however it was built; custom and unknown types stay HashableEvent . The per-type classes only declare their fields (for the type checker): they store, hash, compare, pickle and serialize exactly as this class does. Equality is by type and fields, never by Python class. An event never changes after construction (it is hashed, and its hash is cached): item and attribute assignment, deletion, update , clear , pop , popitem , setdefault and |= raise TypeError; with_fields(**changes) returns a changed copy. Field values should be immutable too: a list or dict inside a game event is hashed by its contents once, so changing it afterwards leaves the cached hash stale. UserDict [ str , Any ]): # ruff: ignore[too-many-public-methods] """Hashable, immutable event class. Hashable events are cacheable, so we can mitigate some of the performance overhead of glitchygames' event subsystem by caching events, which will result in an immediate return if an identical event is encountered, saving some function overhead and processing. Games are welcome to use the built-in pygame event subsystem, but on_*_event callbacks will not be available in that case. The class is chosen by the event's type: ``HashableEvent(pygame.MOUSEMOTION, ...)`` builds a ``MouseMotionEvent`` (``EVENT_CLASSES``), so every event of a type is an instance of that type's class however it was built; custom and unknown types stay ``HashableEvent``. The per-type classes only declare their fields (for the type checker): they store, hash, compare, pickle and serialize exactly as this class does. Equality is by type and fields, never by Python class. An event never changes after construction (it is hashed, and its hash is cached): item and attribute assignment, deletion, ``update``, ``clear``, ``pop``, ``popitem``, ``setdefault`` and ``|=`` raise TypeError; ``with_fields(**changes)`` returns a changed copy. Field values should be immutable too: a list or dict inside a game event is hashed by its contents once, so changing it afterwards leaves the cached hash stale. """ # The cached hash lives in a slot, outside __dict__, so it is never one of the event's # fields (iteration, len, dict(), keys(), __eq__, pickling, to_json; BUGS.md #179 was a # hash stored in __dict__). None until the first __hash__ __slots__ = ( '_content_hash' ,) # Every event has its type (stored in __dict__ with the fields) type : int _content_hash : int | None def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event ) if TYPE_CHECKING : # The constructor's signature for the type checker (UserDict's __init__ takes a # mapping); at run time __init__ is object's def __init__ ( self , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> None : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Declare the constructor's arguments (``__new__`` builds the event).""" else : # Everything is done in __new__; object's __init__ accepts the constructor's arguments # (a class that overrides __new__ but not __init__) and does nothing, without a second # Python call per event __init__ = object . __init__ @staticmethod def from_pygame ( pygame_event : pygame . event . Event ) -> HashableEvent : """Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class (``EVENT_CLASSES``): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds (``HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict)``), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Args: pygame_event: The raw event. Returns: HashableEvent: The event. """ event_type = pygame_event . type event = object . __new__ ( EVENT_CLASSES . get ( event_type , HashableEvent )) fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = event_type fields . update ( pygame_event . dict ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) return event @property def dict ( self : Self ) -> Mapping [ str , Any ]: """A read-only view of the event's type and fields (pygame's ``Event.dict``).""" return MappingProxyType ( self . __dict__ ) def with_fields ( self : Self , ** changes : object ) -> Self : """Return a copy of the event with some fields changed or added (the same class). Args: **changes: The fields to change or add; ``type`` may be given only unchanged. Returns: Self: The changed copy; this event is left as it was. Raises: TypeError: If ``changes`` gives the event another type. """ fields : dict [ str , object ] = { ** self . __dict__ , ** changes } new_type = fields . pop ( 'type' ) if new_type != self . type : raise TypeError ( EVENT_TYPE_CHANGE_MSG . format ( old = self . type , new = new_type )) return self . __class__ ( self . type , ** fields ) def to_json ( self : Self ) -> builtins . dict [ str , JsonValue ]: """Describe the event as JSON: ``{"type": <number>, "attributes": {...}}``. The attributes are encoded as a recording encodes an event's (``glitchygames.recording.json_safe_value``: tuples as lists, lists, dicts, bytes and non-finite floats tagged), except that a window reference is written as None, as a replay serves one. ``from_json`` reverses it. Returns: dict[str, JsonValue]: The JSON-safe description (``json.dumps`` accepts it). """ # Deferred: glitchygames.recording imports the sources and input modules, which import # the events package from glitchygames.recording import ( EVENT_ATTRIBUTES_FIELD , EVENT_TYPE_FIELD , json_safe_value , ) attributes : dict [ str , JsonValue ] = { name : json_safe_value ( None if isinstance ( value , pygame . Window ) else value ) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items () if name != 'type' } return { EVENT_TYPE_FIELD : self . type , EVENT_ATTRIBUTES_FIELD : attributes } @classmethod def from_json ( cls , record : Mapping [ str , JsonValue ]) -> Self : """Build an event from ``to_json``'s description (or a recording's event record). A recorded window reference (a recording's records hold them) becomes None, as a replay serves it. The class is the type's (``EVENT_CLASSES``), as for the constructor. A malformed record raises the recording's ``TraceFormatError`` (``glitchygames.recording.event_from_record``). Args: record: ``{"type": <number>, "attributes": {...}}``, as read back from JSON. Returns: Self: The event. """ # Deferred: glitchygames.recording imports the sources and input modules, which import # the events package from glitchygames.recording import ( WINDOW_REFERENCE , RecordedReference , event_from_record , ) pygame_event = event_from_record ( dict ( record )) attributes = { name : ( None if isinstance ( value , RecordedReference ) and value . kind == WINDOW_REFERENCE else value ) for name , value in pygame_event . dict . items () } return cls ( pygame_event . type , ** attributes ) def _refuse_change ( self : Self , operation : str ) -> NoReturn : """Raise the TypeError every mutator raises. Args: operation: What the caller tried, for the message. Raises: TypeError: Always: events are immutable. """ raise TypeError ( IMMUTABLE_EVENT_MSG . format ( cls = type ( self ) . __name__ , operation = operation )) @override def __setattr__ ( self : Self , name : str , value : object ) -> None : """Refuse: events are immutable (use ``with_fields``).""" self . _refuse_change ( f 'set { name !r} ' ) @override def __delattr__ ( self : Self , name : str ) -> None : """Refuse: events are immutable.""" self . _refuse_change ( f 'delete { name !r} ' ) @override def __setitem__ ( self : Self , key : str , item : object ) -> None : """Refuse: events are immutable (use ``with_fields``).""" self . _refuse_change ( f 'set { key !r} ' ) @override def __getitem__ ( self : Self , key : str ) -> object : """Get an item from the object. Returns: object: The item at the given index. """ return self . __dict__ [ key ] @override def __len__ ( self : Self ) -> int : """Return the length of the object. Returns: int: The number of items. """ return len ( self . __dict__ ) @override def __delitem__ ( self : Self , key : str ) -> None : """Refuse: events are immutable.""" self . _refuse_change ( f 'delete { key !r} ' ) @override def clear ( self : Self ) -> None : """Refuse: events are immutable.""" self . _refuse_change ( 'clear' ) @override def pop ( self : Self , key : str , default : object = None ) -> NoReturn : """Refuse: events are immutable.""" self . _refuse_change ( f 'pop { key !r} ' ) @override def popitem ( self : Self ) -> NoReturn : """Refuse: events are immutable.""" self . _refuse_change ( 'popitem' ) @override def setdefault ( self : Self , key : str , default : object = None ) -> NoReturn : """Refuse: events are immutable (use ``with_fields``).""" self . _refuse_change ( f 'setdefault { key !r} ' ) @override def update ( self : Self , * args : object , ** kwargs : object ) -> None : """Refuse: events are immutable (use ``with_fields``).""" self . _refuse_change ( 'update' ) @override def __ior__ ( self : Self , other : object ) -> NoReturn : """Refuse: events are immutable (``event | changes`` builds a changed copy).""" self . _refuse_change ( '|=' ) @override def __or__ ( self : Self , other : object ) -> Self : """Return a copy with ``other``'s fields changed or added (``with_fields``). UserDict's own ``|`` read ``self.data``, which this class never sets, so it raised AttributeError. Returns: Self: The changed copy, or NotImplemented when ``other`` is not a mapping. """ if not isinstance ( other , Mapping ): return NotImplemented changes = cast ( 'Mapping[str, object]' , other ) return self . with_fields ( ** changes ) @override def __ror__ ( self : Self , other : object ) -> Self : """Return a copy with ``other``'s fields added where the event has none. Returns: Self: The copy (the event's own fields win), or NotImplemented when ``other`` is not a mapping. """ if not isinstance ( other , Mapping ): return NotImplemented additions = cast ( 'Mapping[str, object]' , other ) return self . with_fields ( ** { ** additions , ** self . __dict__ }) @override def copy ( self : Self ) -> Self : """Shallow copy the object. Returns: Self: An equal event of the same class. """ return self . with_fields () def has_key ( self : Self , key : str ) -> bool : """Return True if the key is in the object. Returns: bool: True if has key, False otherwise. """ return key in self . __dict__ # UserDict's own __contains__, __iter__ and get read self.data, which this class never # sets (its items live in __dict__, and an event may have an attribute named `data`), so # they raised or answered from the wrong object (BUGS.md #88). Mapping's items() and # friends go through __iter__ and __getitem__, so they follow these. @override def __contains__ ( self : Self , key : object ) -> bool : """Return True if the event has the attribute `key`. Returns: bool: True if the event has the attribute, False otherwise. """ return key in self . __dict__ @override def __iter__ ( self : Self ) -> Iterator [ str ]: """Iterate over the event's attribute names. Returns: Iterator[str]: The attribute names. """ return iter ( self . __dict__ ) @override def get ( self : Self , key : str , default : Any = None ) -> Any : """Return the event's attribute `key`, or `default` when it has none. Returns: Any: The attribute's value, or `default`. """ return self . __dict__ . get ( key , default ) @override def keys ( self : Self ) -> KeysView [ str ]: """Return the keys of the object. Returns: KeysView[str]: The result. """ return self . __dict__ . keys () @override def values ( self : Self ) -> ValuesView [ Any ]: """Return the values of the object. Returns: bool: The comparison result. Returns: str: The string representation. """ return f ' { self . __class__ . __name__ } ( { self . __dict__ } )' @override def __copy__ ( self : Self ) -> Self : """Shallow copy the object. Returns: Self: The result. """ return self . with_fields () def __deepcopy__ ( self : Self , memo : builtins . dict [ int , Any ]) -> Self : """Deep copy the object. Returns: Self: The result. """ return self . __copy__ () @override def __reduce__ ( self : Self ) -> tuple [ Any , ... ]: """Reduce the object to a picklable form. Returns: tuple: The result. """ # The type is the one required constructor argument (BUGS.md #121) return ( self . __class__ , ( self . type ,), self . __getstate__ ()) @override def __getstate__ ( self : Self ) -> builtins . dict [ str , Any ]: """Return the event's type and fields: the state pickling keeps. object's own ``__getstate__`` would add the slots, so the cached hash: a copy never carries it (it computes its own). Returns: dict[str, Any]: A copy of the type and fields. docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, with_fields ) computes its own. Returns: int ( int ) – The hash value. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, ``with_fields``) computes its own. Returns: int: The hash value. """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

Parameters: **changes ( object , default: {} ) – The fields to change or add; type may be given only unchanged. Returns: Self ( Self ) – The changed copy; this event is left as it was. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 647 648 649 650 651 652 653 654 655 656 657 658 659 660 661 662 663 664 def with_fields ( self : Self , ** changes : object ) -> Self : """Return a copy of the event with some fields changed or added (the same class). docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 1425 1426 1427 1428 1429 1430 1431 1432 1433 1434 1435 1436 1437 1438 1439 1440 1441 1442 1443 1444 1445 1446 1447 1448 1449 1450 1451 1452 1453 1454 1455 1456 1457 1458 1459 1460 1461 1462 1463 1464 1465 1466 1467 1468 1469 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, with_fields ) computes its own. Returns: int ( int ) – The hash value. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 915 916 917 918 919 920 921 922 923 924 925 926 927 928 929 930 931 932 933 934 935 936 937 938 939 940 941 942 943 @override def __hash__ ( self : Self ) -> int : """Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, ``with_fields``) computes its own. Returns: int: The hash value. """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 600 601 602 603 604 605 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )
docs.title: __new__

Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 810 811 812 813 814 815 816 817 818 819 820 821 822 823 824 @override def __or__ ( self : Self , other : object ) -> Self : """Return a copy with ``other``'s fields changed or added (``with_fields``). UserDict's own ``|`` read ``self.data``, which this class never sets, so it raised AttributeError. Returns: Self: The changed copy, or NotImplemented when ``other`` is not a mapping.
